# Video Processor - Flutter

VideoSDK allows you to add custom effects to your video stream before it's transmitted during video calls. This lets you enhance your video in creative ways or achieve specific functionalities.

### Understanding Video Processing

Video processing involves manipulating raw video data (frames) captured by your camera. You can create native processors for Android and iOS to enhance video streams during meetings.

:::info

- Currently, Video Processing is supported only on Android and iOS devices.

:::

### The `VideoProcessor` Interface

The `VideoProcessor` Interface defines a way for your code to interact with the video stream. It essentially lets you intercept each frame before it's sent and apply your processing logic.

#### Key Function: `onFrameReceived`

This is the heart of video processing with VideoSDK. Whenever a new video frame is captured by your camera, the `onFrameReceived` function is called. This function provides you with the raw frame data, allowing you to modify it as needed.

### How it Works:

1. **Implement the Interface:** Create a class that implements the `VideoProcessor` interface. Within this class, define the `onFrameReceived` function.

2. **Process the Frame:** In the `onFrameReceived` function, access the raw video frame data. Apply your desired effects or manipulations to this data.

3. **Return the Processed Frame:** After processing the frame, return the modified version to VideoSDK. This processed frame will then be transmitted during the video call.

4. **Register Your Processor:** Create instances of all the processors you plan to use during the meeting and register them with the `registerVideoProcessor()` method from the `VideoSDK` class during your app's initialization.

5. **Apply the Processor:** Select the desired processor and apply it during the meeting using the `applyVideoProcessor()` method from the `VideoSDK` class to utilize its features.

6. **Remove the Processor:** Stop applying the selected video processor during the meeting, using the `removeVideoProcessor()` method from the `VideoSDK` class allowing you to switch to a different effect or processor as needed.

## API Reference

The API references for all the methods utilized in this guide are provided below.

- [applyVideoProcessor()](https://pub.dev/documentation/videosdk/latest/videosdk/VideoSDK/applyVideoProcessor.html)
- [removeVideoProcessor()](https://pub.dev/documentation/videosdk/latest/videosdk/VideoSDK/removeVideoProcessor.html)

# Cloud Storage Configuration

Use **Cloud Storage Configuration** to choose where recordings and related files for an API key are stored. You can use VideoSDK's default storage or connect a supported cloud-storage provider.

## Open Cloud Storage Configuration

1. Sign in to the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/).
2. Select **RTC** and go to **API Keys**.
3. Find the API key whose storage configuration you want to manage.
4. Select the cube icon in the **Actions** column.

The configuration applies to the selected API key.

## Select a Storage Provider

Select a provider and complete the fields displayed for it.

<Tabs
defaultValue="default"
groupId={"cloud-storage-provider"}
values={[
  {label: 'Default', value: 'default'},
  {label: 'AWS', value: 'aws'},
  {label: 'Azure', value: 'azure'},
  {label: 'GCP', value: 'gcp'},
  {label: 'S3 Compatible', value: 's3-compatible'}
]}>

<TabItem value="default">

Select **Default** to store recordings and files using VideoSDK's managed storage. No external cloud-provider credentials are required.

![Default](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_api_keys_cloud_storage_config_default_1adf77e0fc.png)

### Private Access

Enable **Private Access** to generate temporary URLs for protected file access. Select how long each generated URL should remain valid:

| Expiry | Intended access period |
| --- | --- |
| **15 min** | Quick access |
| **1h** | Temporary access |
| **6h** | Extended session |
| **24h** | Full-day access |

</TabItem>

<TabItem value="aws">

Select **AWS** to store recordings and files in an Amazon S3 bucket.

![AWS](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_api_keys_cloud_storage_config_aws_9ee5c6f5a8.png)

Complete the following fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **AWS Access Key ID** | The access key ID for the AWS identity that can access the bucket. |
| **AWS Secret Access Key** | The secret access key paired with the access key ID. |
| **AWS Region** | The AWS Region containing the bucket, such as `ap-south-1`. |
| **S3 Bucket Name** | The name of the destination S3 bucket. |
| **Bucket Access Level** | The access level applied to stored objects. |

The available bucket access levels include **Public**, **Private**, **Public Read**, **Public Read Write**, **Authenticated Read**, **AWS Exec Read**, **Bucket Owner Read**, and **Bucket Owner Full Control**. Select the level that matches your bucket policy and access requirements.

</TabItem>

<TabItem value="azure">

Select **Azure** to store recordings and files in an Azure Blob Storage container.

![Azure](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_api_keys_cloud_storage_config_azure_22cf72e16f.png)

Complete the following fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Azure Blob Connection String** | The connection string used to authenticate with Azure Blob Storage. |
| **Blob Container Name** | The name of the destination blob container. |

</TabItem>

<TabItem value="gcp">

Select **GCP** to store recordings and files in a Google Cloud Storage bucket.

![GCP](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_api_keys_cloud_storage_config_gcp_b1902c3657.png)

Complete the following fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **GCP Project ID** | The Google Cloud project containing the storage resources. |
| **Service Account Client Email** | The email address of the service account used to access the bucket. |
| **Cloud Storage Bucket Name** | The name of the destination Cloud Storage bucket. |
| **Service Account Private Key** | The private key associated with the service account. |

</TabItem>

<TabItem value="s3-compatible">

Select **S3 Compatible** to use an object-storage service that supports the S3 API.

![S3 Compatible](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_api_keys_cloud_storage_config_s3_compatible_0f7ba132db.png)

Complete the following fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Access Key ID** | The access key ID supplied by the storage provider. |
| **Secret Access Key** | The secret paired with the access key ID. |
| **Region** | The region configured for the storage service. |
| **Bucket Name** | The name of the destination bucket. |
| **Endpoint** | The S3-compatible endpoint URL supplied by the provider. |
| **Bucket Access Level** | The access level applied to stored objects. |

</TabItem>

</Tabs>

## Configure Shared Storage Controls

The controls displayed below the provider fields depend on the selected provider and enabled options.

### Encryption

Enable **Encryption** to encrypt recordings and files before they are stored.

When encryption is enabled:

1. Select the **AES-256-GCM** encryption algorithm.
2. Select **RSA 2048** or **RSA 4096** as the key algorithm.
3. Paste your **Public Key**, or select **Generate Key** to generate one.

Keep the corresponding private key secure. It is required when your workflow needs to decrypt the protected files.

### Fallback Storage

For an external provider, enable **Fallback Storage** to store recordings in VideoSDK's default storage if an upload to the configured provider fails. Recordings stored through fallback storage are billed according to the applicable recording storage charges.

### Data Processing for Transcription & Summaries

Enable **Data Processing for Transcription & Summaries** to allow VideoSDK to process recordings for AI-powered transcription, summaries, and related workflows.

Recordings, transcripts, and processed data are not used to train AI models.

:::important
**Encryption** and **Data Processing for Transcription & Summaries** cannot remain enabled at the same time. Enable encryption when protected storage is required, or enable data processing when VideoSDK must process the recording for transcription and summaries.
:::

## Save the Configuration

Review the provider credentials, destination, access controls, and processing options, then select **Save**.

:::warning
Cloud access keys, connection strings, and service-account private keys are sensitive credentials. Use credentials with only the permissions required for the destination and do not expose them in client-side code, public repositories, screenshots, or logs.
:::

## Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
<summary>Why does one toggle turn off when I enable Encryption or Data Processing?</summary>

The two options are mutually exclusive. Encrypted recordings cannot remain enabled for VideoSDK transcription and summary processing at the same time. Choose **Encryption** for protected storage or **Data Processing for Transcription & Summaries** when you need those processing workflows, then save the configuration.

</details>

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

# Generate API Token

Use **Generate Token** to create a temporary authentication token for a selected API key. Configure the token using the guided options or edit its supported claims in JSON.

:::note
Dashboard-generated tokens are intended for development and testing. In production, keep the API key and secret on a trusted backend and use the VideoSDK Server SDK to generate signed authentication tokens. A client joining a room should receive only its participant token. See [Authentication & Tokens](/server-sdk/authentication-and-tokens).
:::

## Open the Token Generator

1. Sign in to the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/).
2. Select **RTC** and go to **API Keys**.
3. Find the API key that will be used to generate the token.
4. Select the key icon in the **Actions** column.

The **Generate API Token** dialog opens for the selected API key.

## Configure the Token

Choose between **Token Config** for guided configuration and **JSON Editor** for advanced configuration.

<Tabs
defaultValue="token-config"
groupId={"generate-api-token"}
values={[
  {label: 'Token Config', value: 'token-config'},
  {label: 'JSON Editor', value: 'json-editor'}
]}>

<TabItem value="token-config">

Use **Token Config** to select the token's expiry and optional role.

![Generate Token Config](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_api_keys_generate_token_config_3aa35aade1.png)

### Token Expiry

Select how long the generated token should remain valid:

- **7 days**
- **1 month**
- **3 months**
- **6 months**
- **1 year**
- **5 years**

### Role

The optional role controls how the token is intended to be used:

| Role | Intended use |
| --- | --- |
| **Crawler** | Accessing the v2 API. A token with this role cannot be used to run a meeting or room. |
| **RTC** | Running a meeting or room. A token with this role cannot be used with server-side APIs. |
| **None** | Does not assign either of the specialized optional roles. |

</TabItem>

<TabItem value="json-editor">

Use **JSON Editor** when you need to configure the token through supported JSON claims instead of the guided controls.

![Generate Token JSON Editor](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_api_keys_generate_token_json_editor_d8d95bd64c.png)

The editor can include configuration such as:

- **permissions**: The actions permitted by the token, such as `allow_join`.
- **expiresIn**: The token lifetime, such as `7d`.
- **roles**: An optional role list, such as `rtc`.

For example:

```json
{
  "permissions": [
    "allow_join"
  ],
  "expiresIn": "7d",
  "roles": [
    "rtc"
  ]
}
```

Make sure the JSON is valid and contains only supported token configuration before regenerating the token.

</TabItem>

</Tabs>

## Apply Configuration Changes

Changing the expiry, role, or JSON configuration does not modify the token that is currently displayed. Select **Regenerate Token** after every configuration change to generate a token containing the updated values.

After regeneration, the confirmation message identifies the selected expiry and role when applicable.

## Copy the Token

When **Your Token Is Ready** appears:

1. Select the copy icon beside the generated token.
2. Store the token securely.
3. Use the token only in the application or service for which it was generated.

The generated token is temporary and cannot be viewed again after the dialog is closed. Select **Cancel** or close the dialog only after copying the token you need.

:::warning
Generated tokens grant access according to their configuration. Do not expose them in client-side source code, public repositories, screenshots, or logs.
:::

## Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
<summary>Why does my token still have the previous expiry or role?</summary>

Selecting a different expiry or role only changes the pending configuration. Select **Regenerate Token**, then copy and use the newly displayed token.

</details>

<details>
<summary>What should I do if I closed the dialog before copying the token?</summary>

The previously displayed token cannot be revealed again from the dialog. Open **Generate Token**, confirm the required configuration, select **Regenerate Token**, and copy the newly generated token before closing the dialog.

</details>

# API Key Settings

Use **Settings** to define fallback bandwidth, recording, streaming, integration, processing, and access-control behavior for sessions that use a selected API key.

## Open Settings

1. Sign in to the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/).
2. Select **RTC** and go to **API Keys**.
3. Find the API key whose settings you want to manage.
4. Select the gear icon in the **Actions** column.

The page header identifies the selected API key and shows when its settings were last updated.

:::important
Dashboard settings act as fallback configuration. If the same option is supplied through an API request, the value passed through the API takes higher priority.
:::

Use the navigation panel on the left to move between settings sections. Select **Save** after making the required changes.

## Maximum Send Bitrate

**Maximum Send Bitrate Per Participant** limits the total upload bandwidth used by all media streams sent by one participant.

![Maximum Send Bitrate](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_api_keys_maximum_send_bitrate_d2c4912e9c.png)

| Option | Maximum send bitrate |
| --- | --- |
| **Auto** | Removes the configured upload limit. |
| **SD** | 800 kbps |
| **HD** | 1500 kbps |
| **Full HD** | 3000 kbps |

Choose a limit that suits the expected network conditions and media quality.

## Recording Settings

Enable **Recording Settings** to define the fallback recording configuration for sessions using the API key.

![Recording Settings](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_api_keys_recording_settings_3e7c9cca71.png)

| Setting | Available options or behavior |
| --- | --- |
| **Enabled Modes** | Allow **Video & Audio**, **Audio Only**, or both recording modes. |
| **Start Recording Automatically** | Start recording automatically when the applicable session begins. |
| **Layout Style** | **Grid**, **Spotlight**, or **Sidebar**. |
| **Who to Prioritize** | **Active Speaker** or **Pinned Participant**. |
| **Maximum Tiles In Grid** | Select the maximum number of participant tiles, from 1 through 25. |
| **Theme** | **System Default**, **Light**, or **Dark**. |
| **Video Orientation** | **Landscape** or **Portrait**. |
| **Recording Quality** | **SD (Low)**, **HD (Medium)**, or **Full HD (High)**. |
| **Recording Mode** | **Video & Audio** or **Audio Only**. |

Layout, participant priority, tile count, theme, and orientation primarily affect composed video output. Select an audio-only mode when video composition is not required.

## HLS Streaming Settings

Enable **HLS Streaming Settings** to define how sessions are streamed through HLS.

![HLS Streaming Settings](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_api_keys_hls_streaming_568ad2bf06.png)

| Setting | Available options or behavior |
| --- | --- |
| **Enabled Modes** | Allow **Video & Audio**, **Audio Only**, or both streaming modes. |
| **Auto Start HLS** | Start HLS automatically for an applicable session. |
| **Record HLS Stream** | Save a recording of the HLS stream. |
| **Layout Style** | **Grid**, **Spotlight**, or **Sidebar**. |
| **Who to Prioritize** | **Active Speaker** or **Pinned Participant**. |
| **Maximum Tiles In Grid** | Select the maximum number of participant tiles, from 1 through 25. |
| **Theme** | **System Default**, **Light**, or **Dark**. |
| **HLS Orientation** | **Landscape** or **Portrait**. |
| **HLS Quality** | **SD (Low)**, **HD (Medium)**, or **Full HD (High)**. |
| **HLS Streaming Mode** | **Video & Audio** or **Audio Only**. |

## RTMP Output

![RTMP Output, SIP Integration, Realtime Translation and Transcription & Summary](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_api_keys_rtmp_sip_realtimetranslation_transsummary_b0e517acfc.png)

Enable **RTMP Output** to allow sessions using the API key to stream to external RTMP destinations.

This toggle provides the fallback availability setting. The destination and other stream-specific values are supplied when the RTMP stream is configured.

## SIP Integration

Enable **SIP Integration** to allow sessions using the API key to manage external calls through SIP.

Disable the setting when applications using this API key should not use the fallback SIP integration.

## Realtime Translation

Enable **Realtime Translation** to allow live translation for multilingual conversations.

The languages and translation behavior used by a session depend on its runtime configuration.

## Transcription & Summary

Enable **Transcription & Summary** to allow AI transcription for sessions using the API key.

| Setting | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Enabled** | Enables transcription and summary configuration. |
| **Enable Summary** | Generates a summary in addition to the transcription. |
| **Summary Style Instructions** | Provides instructions for the desired summary structure or focus, such as highlighting decisions, action items, and owners. |

Write clear summary instructions describing the information and format required. Summary settings are available when the feature and its required processing configuration are enabled.

## Whitelist Domain

Use **Whitelist Domain** to restrict API-key usage to requests originating from approved domains.

![Whitelist Domain](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_api_keys_whitelist_domain_83b18d6df9.png)

1. Enter the domain after the `https://` prefix.
2. Select **Add Domain**.
3. Add each additional approved domain separately.
4. Select **Save** to apply the updated whitelist.

Enter only domains that should be allowed to use the selected API key. Confirm the hostname carefully so legitimate application requests are not blocked.

## Save Settings

After reviewing all sections, select **Save**. The updated-by information in the header identifies the user and time associated with the latest saved configuration.

## Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
<summary>Why was a saved dashboard setting not used for my session?</summary>

Check whether the same option was included in the API request that created or configured the session. Values passed through the API take priority, so the dashboard value is used only when the request does not override it.

</details>

import { AgentCardGrid } from '@site/src/components/agent/cards';

# API Keys

The **API Keys** page lists the credentials created for your organization. Use it to create API keys, control whether a key is active, reveal its secret, and open token, storage, or feature settings for a selected key.

![API Keys Table](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_api_keys_table_7682d5dbb8.png)

## Open API Keys

To access the page:

1. Sign in to the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/).
2. Select **RTC**.
3. Select **[API Keys](https://app.videosdk.live/api-keys)** from the navigation sidebar.

## Create an API Key

Select **Add New API key** to open the **Create New API Key** dialog.

1. Enter a **Key Name** containing only letters and spaces.
2. Make sure the name contains between 3 and 42 characters.
3. Select **Generate key**.

Select **Cancel** or close the dialog to return without creating a key.

## Find an API Key

Use **Search** to find a key by its name or other searchable information displayed in the list.

## API Keys Table

Each row represents an API key created for the organization.

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Key Name** | The descriptive name assigned when the key was created. |
| **API key** | The masked API key. Its final characters remain visible to help identify the credential. |
| **Secret** | The masked secret associated with the API key. Select the eye icon to reveal it. |
| **Cloud Storage** | The cloud storage configuration associated with the key. **Default** means recordings are stored using VideoSDK's default storage. |
| **Status** | Indicates whether the API key is active. Use the toggle to enable or disable it. |
| **Created At** | The date and time when the API key was created. |
| **Actions** | Opens token generation, cloud-storage configuration, and settings for the selected key. |

## Generate Authentication Tokens Securely

Your API key and its corresponding secret are server-side credentials used to generate and sign authentication tokens. With the VideoSDK Server SDK, tokens are signed locally on your backend, so the secret does not need to be sent over the network.

The Server SDK uses:

- **Management tokens** to authenticate server-side API requests.
- **Participant tokens** to authorize a client application to join a room.

For production applications, use the following secure flow:

1. Keep the API key and secret in secure server-side storage.
2. Initialize the Server SDK on your backend with the API key and secret.
3. Generate the required management or participant token with its expiry, permissions, role, and optional access restrictions.
4. For a participant token, let the client request the generated token from your backend.
5. Use the generated token—not the API key or secret—in the client application.

This flow prevents the secret from being exposed in a browser, mobile application, or other client environment. Use the Dashboard's **Generate Token** action for temporary development or testing tokens.

For implementation examples in Node.js, Go, and Rust, see [Authentication & Tokens](/server-sdk/authentication-and-tokens).

:::warning
Treat API keys, secrets, generated tokens, and storage credentials as sensitive information. Do not expose them in client-side code, public repositories, screenshots, or logs.
:::

## Manage an API Key

The actions at the end of each row apply to that specific API key:

<AgentCardGrid
cards={[
{
title: "Generate Token",
description: "Generate a temporary authentication token using guided options or a JSON configuration.",
link: "./api-keys/generate-token"
},
{
title: "Cloud Storage Configuration",
description: "Choose the storage provider and configure storage, access, encryption, fallback, and data-processing options.",
link: "./api-keys/cloud-storage-configuration"
},
{
title: "Settings",
description: "Manage bandwidth, recording, streaming, integrations, transcription, translation, and access controls.",
link: "./api-keys/settings"
}
]}
columns={3}
/>

## Enable or Disable an API Key

Use the **Status** toggle to control whether the key is active. Disabling a key can interrupt applications or services that use it, so confirm that the credential is no longer required before turning it off.

:::note
The information and actions available for an API key can depend on your organization, enabled products, and the key's current configuration.
:::

## Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
<summary>How are the API key and secret used to generate an authentication token?</summary>

The API key identifies the VideoSDK account in the JWT payload, while its matching secret signs the token locally on your backend. The Server SDK can use these credentials to create management tokens for server-side API requests or participant tokens for joining rooms. Provide only the participant token—not the API key or secret—to the client. See [Authentication & Tokens](/server-sdk/authentication-and-tokens) for Node.js, Go, and Rust examples.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How can I rotate an API key without interrupting my application?</summary>

Create a replacement API key and update your server-side applications to use the new credentials. Verify that the replacement works before disabling the previous key. Keeping the old key active during verification helps avoid an immediate interruption.

</details>

<details>
<summary>What should I do if an API key or secret is exposed?</summary>

Stop using the exposed credential, create a replacement, and update every service that used it. Disable the exposed API key after moving those services to the replacement. Also remove the credential from source code, logs, screenshots, and repository history where applicable.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why did authentication stop working for an existing integration?</summary>

Confirm that the integration is using the intended API key and its corresponding secret, and check that the key's **Status** toggle is enabled. Authentication can fail if a different key and secret are combined or if the selected key has been disabled.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How should I organize API keys for multiple applications or environments?</summary>

Use separately named keys for independent applications or environments, such as development, staging, and production. This makes each credential easier to identify and allows you to replace or disable one key without changing every integration.

</details>

# Billing Add-ons

The **Add-ons** tab lists optional capabilities that can be added to your organization for a recurring monthly charge. Use it to review available add-ons, prepare a selection, and confirm the current-month and recurring totals before continuing to payment.

![Billing Add-ons](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_billing_add_ons_3ff42a663a.png)

:::note
Add-ons are currently in **Beta**. Availability, behavior, and pricing can change while the feature is in beta.
:::

## Open Billing Add-ons

To access the page:

1. Sign in to the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/).
2. Select **RTC**.
3. Select **[Billing](https://app.videosdk.live/profile/billing)** from the navigation sidebar.
4. Select **Add-ons**.

## Available Add-ons

Each add-on card displays its name, purpose, monthly price, and an action for including or removing it from the current selection.

| Add-on | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **HIPAA Compliance** | Adds healthcare-focused data security and compliance capabilities. |
| **GDPR Compliance** | Adds controls intended for EU data privacy and protection requirements. |
| **SOC 2 Type II** | Adds controls associated with security, availability, and confidentiality. |
| **ISO 27001** | Adds capabilities associated with the international information-security management standard. |
| **Geo-fencing (Geo Restriction)** | Unlocks region-based access controls that can be configured for individual API keys. |
| **Cloud Proxy** | Provides secure traffic routing through private network controls. |
| **CERT-IN Compliance** | Adds capabilities associated with India's cybersecurity guidelines. |

The add-ons and prices available to your organization are shown directly in the dashboard. Prices are displayed in INR for organizations registered in India and USD for organizations registered outside India.

## Select Add-ons

To prepare an add-on purchase:

1. Select **Add** on each add-on you want to include.
2. Review the highlighted add-on cards. Their action changes to **Remove**.
3. Select **Remove** if you want to exclude an add-on before continuing.
4. Review the total displayed at the bottom of the page.
5. Select **Continue** to proceed to confirmation and payment.

Selecting or removing an add-on updates the order total. The change is not complete until you continue through the remaining confirmation and payment steps.

## Configure Geo-fencing After Purchase

The Geo-fencing configuration becomes available only after the **Geo-fencing (Geo Restriction)** add-on has been purchased.

After the purchase is active:

1. Open **API Keys** in the Dashboard.
2. Find the API key whose access you want to restrict.
3. Select **Settings** for that API key.
4. Locate the Geo-fencing settings and select the permitted region.
5. Save the API key settings.

Geo-fencing is configured separately for each API key. If the Geo-fencing settings do not appear, confirm that the add-on purchase was completed for the current organization.

## Review the Order Total

When one or more add-ons are selected, the total section summarizes two billing periods:

- **Current month**: Shows the prorated charge for the remainder of the current billing month.
- **Next month onwards**: Shows the full recurring monthly charge for the selected add-ons.

Select or hover over the information icon beside **Total** to review the charge for each selected add-on and the subtotal for both periods.

Applicable taxes, such as GST, are displayed separately from the subtotal. Review the complete amount before selecting **Continue**.

:::note
The current-month charge can be lower than the displayed monthly price because it is prorated according to the time remaining in the current billing month.
:::

## Add-on Pricing and Currency

The dashboard is the current source of truth for add-on availability and pricing. The displayed currency is based on the country selected when the organization was created:

| Signup country | Billing currency |
| --- | --- |
| India | Indian rupee (INR) |
| Any country outside India | United States dollar (USD) |

Taxes and the final payable total can vary based on the organization's billing information and applicable regulations.

## Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
<summary>Why is the current-month total lower than the listed monthly price?</summary>

The dashboard prorates the first charge according to the time remaining in the current billing month. The **Next month onwards** section shows the full recurring monthly amount.

</details>

# Billing History

The **Billing History** tab provides a record of your organization's payments, invoices, credit purchases, reloads, subscriptions, and other billing activity. The available records depend on the organization's billing model and completed transactions.

## Open Billing History

To access the page:

1. Sign in to the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/).
2. Select **RTC**.
3. Select **[Billing](https://app.videosdk.live/profile/billing)** from the navigation sidebar.
4. Select **Billing History**.

## Prepaid and Postpaid History

Use the selector at the top of the page to switch between the two billing models:

| View | Applies to | What it contains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Prepaid** | Current **Pay As You Go (On-Demand)** organizations | Credit purchases, automatic reloads, subscriptions, payments, and related prepaid activity. |
| **Postpaid** | Legacy Pay As You Go organizations and Enterprise organizations configured for postpaid billing | Invoices generated for completed billing periods, including their due dates and payment status. |

An organization may have records in only one view. Switching to a billing model that has not been used can display an empty history.

## Filter Prepaid History

![Billing History Prepaid](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_billing_billhistory_prepaid_b8d1524570.png)

The **Prepaid** view supports the following filters:

- **Type**: Show one or more transaction types.
  - **Credit top-up**: Funds added manually to the organization's wallet.
  - **Credit reload**: Funds added through an automatic reload.
  - **Subscription**: Charges associated with recurring subscriptions, add-ons, or usage-limit packs.
- **Date range**: Show transactions completed within a selected period.

Select the required values and apply the filter. Filters affect only the records displayed in the table and do not modify the underlying billing history.

## Understand Prepaid Records

Each prepaid entry can contain:

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Invoice No.** | The identifier assigned to the billing entry or invoice. |
| **Date** | The date on which the transaction was recorded. |
| **Amount** | The transaction amount in the organization's billing currency. |
| **Type** | The billing activity, such as a credit top-up, credit reload, or subscription. |
| **Status** | The current payment or transaction state, such as **Paid**. |
| **Payment Method** | The method used for the transaction, when available. |
| **Actions** | Opens the operations available for that billing entry. |

A dash indicates that information is unavailable or does not apply to that entry. For example, a wallet adjustment may not show a credit card as its payment method.

An amount prefixed with a minus sign represents a negative billing entry, such as a credit, reversal, or adjustment. Review the corresponding entry or invoice to confirm why the amount was applied.

## View and Download an Invoice

For a billing entry that provides an invoice:

1. Open the three-dot menu in the **Actions** column.
2. Select **View** to open the invoice details page.

![Billing History Details](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_billing_billhistory_details_a5237b06d3.png)

The details page provides an itemized breakdown of the invoice. Depending on the transaction, it can include:

- The invoice number and billing month.
- The payment date and payment method.
- Line-item descriptions, quantities, unit prices, and amounts.
- The subtotal and applicable taxes.
- The invoice total, applied wallet balance, and final amount charged.

Select **Download PDF** to download a PDF copy of the invoice for accounting, reconciliation, or record keeping. The exact fields and tax breakdown depend on the billing entry and the organization's billing country.

## Filter and Review Postpaid History

![Billing History Postpaid](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_billing_billhistory_postpaid_f87cf48647.png)

The **Postpaid** view supports filtering by **Date range**. Its table is organized around monthly invoices and can contain:

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Invoice No.** | The identifier assigned to the postpaid invoice. |
| **Month** | The usage or billing month covered by the invoice. |
| **Due Date** | The date by which payment is due. |
| **Amount** | The invoiced amount in the organization's billing currency. |
| **Status** | The current invoice state, such as **Paid**. |
| **Payment Method** | The recorded payment method, when available. |
| **Actions** | Opens the operations available for that invoice. |

Postpaid records appear only for organizations that were billed through a postpaid account arrangement.

## Billing Currency

Amounts are displayed in the billing currency determined by the country selected when the organization was created:

- Organizations registered in India use **INR**.
- Organizations registered outside India use **USD**.

The signup country is locked and cannot be changed from the billing address.

## When No History Is Available

The page remains empty until qualifying billing activity occurs. A newly created organization, a Free organization that has not completed a transaction, or an organization viewing an unused billing model may not have any records.

Recent transactions also appear on the **Overview** tab under **Last 5 billing history**. The complete record is available on the **Billing History** tab.

## Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
<summary>Why is Prepaid history available but Postpaid history is empty?</summary>

The current Pay As You Go (On-Demand) model is prepaid. Postpaid history is populated only for legacy Pay As You Go accounts and Enterprise organizations configured for postpaid billing.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why does a billing entry show a negative amount?</summary>

A negative amount represents a credit, reversal, or adjustment applied to the billing account. Review the corresponding entry or invoice for its specific context.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why is a recent transaction not visible?</summary>

Check whether the correct **Prepaid** or **Postpaid** view is selected, then clear or adjust the type and date-range filters. A transaction may also take time to appear while its payment status is being processed.

</details>

# Billing Overview

The **Overview** tab summarizes your organization's active plan, wallet balance, recent usage charges, saved payment method, and latest billing activity. The sections shown on this page depend on whether you have added a card, used a billable service, or completed a transaction.

![Billing Overview](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_billing_overview_cac5f7770d.png)

## Open Billing Overview

To access the page:

1. Sign in to the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/).
2. Select **RTC**.
3. Select **[Billing](https://app.videosdk.live/profile/billing)** from the navigation sidebar.
4. Select **Overview**.

The Billing section also contains separate tabs for **Plans**, **Add-ons**, **Usage Limits**, **Payment Details**, **Billing History**, and **Spend Info**.

## Active Plan and Wallet Balance

The balance panel displays:

- Your organization's active plan, such as **Free** or **Pay As You Go - On Demand**.
- The current prepaid wallet balance available to pay for usage.
- Preset amounts that can be added to the wallet.
- A custom amount field for entering a different top-up amount.

To add funds:

1. Select a preset amount or enter a custom amount.
2. Select **Add Fund**.
3. Complete the payment flow.

The dashboard displays the minimum top-up amount beside the controls. In the current dashboard, the minimum is ₹1,000 for INR billing and $10 for USD billing.

## Billing Currency

The billing currency is determined by the country selected when the organization is first created:

| Signup country | Billing currency |
| --- | --- |
| India | Indian rupee (INR) |
| Any country outside India | United States dollar (USD) |

Preset top-up amounts, custom amounts, balances, charges, and invoices are displayed in the organization's billing currency.

## Auto Reload

Enable **Auto Reload** to automatically add funds when the wallet balance falls below the configured threshold. This helps prevent service interruption caused by an insufficient balance.

:::note
Auto Reload is currently unavailable for cards issued in India because of RBI regulations. Indian organizations can continue to add funds manually.
:::

## Spend Info

The **Spend Info** preview shows how wallet funds are consumed across products and usage. Free-plan users can use this section to review charges deducted from their available credit.

When spending data is available, each entry can show:

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Description** | The product, feature, or metered usage that generated the charge. |
| **Usage** | The measured quantity for the entry. |
| **Rate** | The rate applied to the measured usage. |
| **Amount** | The amount deducted from the wallet for the entry. |

Select **See All** to open the complete **Spend Info** tab. Spend data in the updated dashboard is available by month starting from **January 2026**.

If the organization has not incurred any usage-based charges, the section displays **No spending activity yet**.

## Payment Details

After you add a card, the **Payment Details** section displays the saved card and billing-address information. Select **Manage Card** to open the complete **Payment Details** tab.

If no card has been added, the section displays **No payment method added**. Select **Add New Card** to add one.

## Recent Billing History

After the organization completes a billing transaction, the Overview page displays the five most recent entries under **Last 5 billing history**. Select **See All** to open the complete **Billing History** tab.

If the organization has not completed any billing activity, the section displays **No billing history yet**.

Billing history is separated by account model:

- **Prepaid**: Used for the current **Pay As You Go (On-Demand)** plan, where funds are added before usage.
- **Postpaid**: Used for legacy Pay As You Go accounts and Enterprise organizations configured for postpaid billing.

## Usage Limits

VideoSDK limits supported services by concurrent usage rather than total lifetime usage. Open **Billing** > **Usage Limits** to review current limits, realtime usage, maximum concurrent requests, and available add-on packs.

For an explanation of concurrency and the available limits, see [Understanding Usage Quota Limits](../../quotas-and-limit-new.md).

## Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
<summary>Why is my organization billed in INR instead of USD?</summary>

The billing currency is based on the country selected when the organization was first created. Organizations registered in India use INR, while organizations registered outside India use USD.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why are Payment Details or Billing History empty?</summary>

**Payment Details** remains empty until a card is added. **Billing History** remains empty until the organization completes a billing transaction. These sections populate automatically when the corresponding information becomes available.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why can I not enable Auto Reload for my card?</summary>

Auto Reload is unavailable for cards issued in India because of RBI regulations. Add funds manually when you need to replenish the wallet balance.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why can I not find spend data from before January 2026?</summary>

Monthly Spend Info in the updated dashboard starts from January 2026. Earlier months are not available in this view.

</details>

# Payment Details

The **Payment Details** tab contains the payment methods and billing-address information associated with your organization. Use this page to add a card, review the default payment method, and keep the editable billing details up to date.

![Billing Payment Details](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_billing_payment_details_34b51d8efa.png)

## Open Payment Details

To access the page:

1. Sign in to the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/).
2. Select **RTC**.
3. Select **[Billing](https://app.videosdk.live/profile/billing)** from the navigation sidebar.
4. Select **Payment Details**.

## Payment Method

The **Payment Method** section displays the cards saved for your organization. Card details are masked, and the card currently used for payments is marked **Default**.

If no card has been added, the page displays **No payment method added**.

### Add a Card

To add a payment method:

1. Select **Add New Card** or **Add new**.
2. Enter the card number, expiration date, and security code.
3. Enter the name shown on the card.
4. Select **Continue** and complete any verification requested by the card issuer or payment provider.

After the card is added successfully, it appears in the **Payment Method** section. When multiple cards are available, make sure a working card is configured as the default payment method.

:::note
Never share complete card details, security codes, or payment-verification information with another person. The Dashboard masks stored card information when displaying it.
:::

## Resolve a Payment-Method Issue

When the Dashboard detects a problem with a saved card, it displays a **Payment Issue** notice. Review the saved payment method and add or update a working card. If multiple cards are saved, set the card that should be charged as the default payment method.

A card can still be declined by its issuer because of insufficient funds, online or international payment restrictions, an expired card, or a failed verification step. Contact the card issuer if the entered information is correct but the payment continues to fail.

## Billing Address

The **Billing Address** section is used for invoicing, tax calculation, and payment verification. Depending on the organization, it can display:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Business Legal Name** | The legal name associated with the billing account. |
| **Billing Email** | The email address used for billing communication. |
| **Address Line 1 and 2** | The organization's billing street address. |
| **City** | The billing city. |
| **State** | The billing state or region. |
| **Country** | The country selected when the organization was created. |
| **Post Code** | The postal or ZIP code for the billing address. |

Select **Edit billing address** to update the editable address fields, then save the changes.

:::important
The organization's country is selected during signup and is locked afterward. It cannot be changed from the billing address. Contact VideoSDK if the organization was created with an incorrect country or if the account must be moved to another billing country.
:::

## Billing Country and Currency

The locked signup country determines the organization's billing currency:

| Signup country | Billing currency |
| --- | --- |
| India | Indian rupee (INR) |
| Any country outside India | United States dollar (USD) |

Editing the street address, city, state, postal code, business name, or billing email does not change the billing country or currency.

## Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
<summary>Why can I not change the country in my billing address?</summary>

The country is selected when the organization is created and is locked afterward because it determines the organization's billing currency and regional billing setup. Other editable billing-address fields can still be updated. Create a new account if want the account with a different country..

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why is my card not working?</summary>

Confirm that the card details are current and that the intended card is the default payment method. The card issuer can also decline online or international transactions, reject a verification attempt, or block a transaction because of account restrictions. Contact the issuer if the information is correct and the payment continues to fail.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why did my billing currency not change after I edited the address?</summary>

Billing currency is determined by the locked country selected during signup. Changing editable address fields does not change the organization's country or currency.

</details>

# Billing Plans

The **Plans** tab shows the plans available to your organization and identifies its active plan. Use this page to move from the Free plan to usage-based billing or to contact VideoSDK about an Enterprise plan.

![Billing Plans](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_billing_plans_a5e8c75368.png)

## Open Billing Plans

To access the page:

1. Sign in to the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/).
2. Select **RTC**.
3. Select **[Billing](https://app.videosdk.live/profile/billing)** from the navigation sidebar.
4. Select **Plans**.

## Available Plans

The page displays the following plan options:

| Plan | Best suited for | Dashboard action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Free** | Exploring VideoSDK, testing an integration, and getting started without adding a credit card. | The card displays **Active** when this is the organization's current plan. |
| **Pay As You Go (On-Demand)** | Production usage that should be charged according to consumption. | Select **Add Credit** to begin the payment flow and fund the wallet. |
| **Enterprise** | High-volume or customized requirements, including negotiated limits, support, deployment, or commercial terms. | Select **Contact Sales** to discuss requirements with VideoSDK. |

Each plan card provides a short summary and selected feature or pricing highlights. The active plan is visually outlined and marked as active.

## Move to Pay As You Go

To move from the Free plan to **Pay As You Go (On-Demand)**:

1. Locate the **Pay As You Go (On-Demand)** card.
2. Select **Add Credit**.
3. Add or confirm the required billing information.
4. Select an amount and complete the payment.

After the payment succeeds, the funds are added to the organization's prepaid wallet. Usage charges are deducted from that balance.

:::note
The amount and currency shown during payment depend on the organization's billing country. Organizations registered in India use INR, while organizations registered outside India use USD.
:::

## Choose an Enterprise Plan

Select **Contact Sales** on the Enterprise card when your organization needs custom pricing, higher concurrency, dedicated support, private deployment options, or other negotiated requirements.

VideoSDK works with the organization to define the applicable limits, features, support arrangements, and commercial terms.

## Compare Current Plans and Pricing

Select **View Detailed Plans** to open the complete plan comparison. For the latest rates, included credit, supported features, and Enterprise options, see [VideoSDK Pricing](https://videosdk.live/pricing).

For answers to common questions about plans, usage calculations, credits, and charges, see the [Pricing FAQ](../../pricing-new-faq.md).

:::note
Prices and plan inclusions can change. Use the pricing page and the values displayed in your dashboard as the current source of truth.
:::

## Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
<summary>Why are the prices or currency in my dashboard different from an example?</summary>

The dashboard uses the organization's billing currency, which is determined by the country selected when the organization was first created. India-based organizations use INR, while organizations outside India use USD. Current prices can also change over time, so refer to the values displayed in your dashboard.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why does the Enterprise plan not show a fixed price?</summary>

Enterprise pricing is customized around the organization's usage, concurrency, support, deployment, and commercial requirements. Select **Contact Sales** to receive an applicable configuration and quote.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why does the Free plan not have an upgrade button?</summary>

When Free is the organization's current plan, its card is marked **Active**. Use **Add Credit** on the Pay As You Go card to begin moving to usage-based billing, or select **Contact Sales** for Enterprise.

</details>

# Spend Info

The **Spend Info** tab shows how your organization's wallet balance is consumed across VideoSDK products and metered services. Use it to review the measured usage, applied rate, and resulting wallet deduction for each usage category.

![Billing Spend Info](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_billing_spend_info_7f791bfcfe.png)


## Open Spend Info

To access the page:

1. Sign in to the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/).
2. Select **RTC**.
3. Select **[Billing](https://app.videosdk.live/profile/billing)** from the navigation sidebar.
4. Select **Spend Info**.

Free-plan organizations can also use this page to review usage deducted from their available free credit.

## Select a Month

Use the **Months** filter to select the billing month you want to inspect. Monthly Spend Info in the updated Dashboard is available from **January 2026** onward.

The table refreshes when another month is selected. Only usage assigned to the selected month appears in the results.

## Search and Navigate Results

Use the available controls to find and review entries:

- Enter a product, model, or usage name in **Search** to narrow the table.
- Use **Previous**, **Next**, or a page number to move between result pages.
- Change the number of rows displayed per page when more or fewer entries should be visible at once.

Search and pagination affect only the displayed results. They do not change billing data.

## Understand Spend Entries

Each row represents a metered product or usage category:

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Description** | The VideoSDK product, feature, model, storage operation, or metered service that generated the charge. |
| **Usage** | The measured quantity consumed during the selected month. |
| **Rate** | The billing rate applied to each unit of measured usage. |
| **Amount** | The total amount deducted from the wallet for that entry. |

The measurement unit depends on the product. Examples can include:

- RTC audio or video minutes
- HLS encoding or viewer minutes
- File encoding and storage
- Speech-to-text minutes
- AI model input or output usage
- Other VideoSDK services enabled for the organization

The product name or model can be included in **Description** when multiple variants are billed at different rates.

## Understand Amounts and Precision

Spend amounts are displayed with a minus sign because they represent deductions from the organization's prepaid wallet balance. For example, `-₹100` means ₹100 was deducted for that usage category.

Usage, rates, and calculated amounts can contain different numbers of decimal places. Very small per-unit rates can therefore produce an amount with greater precision than a typical currency display.

:::note
The rate and amount shown in the Dashboard use the organization's billing currency. Organizations registered in India use INR, while organizations registered outside India use USD.
:::

## Spend Info and Billing History

**Spend Info** and **Billing History** answer different questions:

| Page | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **Spend Info** | Explains which products and measured usage consumed wallet funds. |
| **Billing History** | Records payments, credit additions, reloads, subscriptions, invoices, and other billing transactions. |

Adding funds appears in **Billing History**, while using those funds appears as product-level deductions in **Spend Info**.

## When No Spending Is Available

If the organization has not incurred any metered charges during the selected month, the page displays an empty state such as **No spending activity yet**.

An empty result can also appear when a search does not match any entries. Clear the search and confirm that the intended month is selected before concluding that no usage was recorded.

## Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
<summary>Why can I not select a month before January 2026?</summary>

Spend Info in the updated Dashboard is available by month starting from January 2026. Earlier usage is not exposed through this view.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why does the Amount column contain negative values?</summary>

The values represent money deducted from the organization's wallet for metered usage. Payments and funds added to the wallet are recorded separately under **Billing History**.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why does a calculated amount contain many decimal places?</summary>

Some services use very small per-unit rates or highly granular usage measurements. Multiplying that usage by the applicable rate can produce an amount with greater decimal precision.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why is recent usage missing from Spend Info?</summary>

Confirm that the correct month is selected and clear any active search. Recently completed usage may also take time to be processed and added to the billing ledger.

</details>

# Usage Limits

The **Usage Limits** tab shows the concurrent capacity available to your organization. Use it to monitor realtime usage, review recent peak demand, and purchase additional capacity for supported services.

![Billing Usage Limits](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_billing_usage_limits_bbf75457d6.png)

## Open Usage Limits

To access the page:

1. Sign in to the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/).
2. Select **RTC**.
3. Select **[Billing](https://app.videosdk.live/profile/billing)** from the navigation sidebar.
4. Select **Usage Limits**.

## How Concurrent Limits Work

Usage limits apply to simultaneous activity across the entire organization, not to the total activity accumulated during a month.

For example, an organization with a limit of 50 concurrent hosts can run multiple meetings at the same time, but no more than 50 hosts can be active across those meetings at once. When the limit is reached, another request cannot be processed until capacity becomes available or the limit is increased.

## Default Limits and Packs

Default limits depend on the organization's plan. Supported Pay As You Go organizations can purchase packs to increase their concurrent capacity.

| Service | Free plan | Pay As You Go (On-Demand) | Capacity added per pack | Maximum packs on Dashboard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Participants (Hosts)** | 50 concurrent hosts | 500 concurrent hosts | 100 hosts | 5 |
| **Recordings** | 1 concurrent recording | 10 concurrent recordings | 10 recordings | 5 |
| **Agent Cloud Sessions** | 1 concurrent session | 10 concurrent sessions | 10 sessions | 5 |
| **Viewers (HLS/RTC)** | 100 concurrent viewers | 200 concurrent viewers | 200 viewers | 10 |
| **HLS Encoding** | 1 concurrent encoding | 10 concurrent encodings | 10 encodings | 5 |
| **SIP Connect** | 1 concurrent connection | 10 concurrent connections | 10 connections | 5 |
| **Realtime Transcription** | 1 concurrent transcription | 10 concurrent transcriptions | 10 transcriptions | 5 |
| **RTMP** | 1 concurrent stream | 10 concurrent streams | 10 streams | 5 |

<!-- | **VideoSDK Inference** | Upgrade to Pay As You Go | 5 concurrent units | Contact Sales | Not available | -->

### Default Per-Room Limits

These limits apply to each individual room and are separate from the organization-wide concurrency limits above.

| Limit | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Active speakers | 15 |
| Participants | 100 |
| Interactive Live Streaming viewers | 1,000 |
| HTTP Live Streaming viewers | 200 |

The dashboard displays the current pack price in the organization's billing currency. Organizations registered in India use INR, while organizations registered outside India use USD.

:::note
Limits, pack sizes, prices, and purchase maximums can change. Use the values displayed in your dashboard as the current source of truth.
:::

## Understand a Usage-Limit Card

Each service card summarizes the configured limit and observed usage:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Current** | The concurrent capacity included with the current plan or configuration. |
| **Added** | The additional capacity selected or purchased through packs. |
| **Total** | The combined concurrent capacity after applying the added packs. |
| **Usage** | The organization's current realtime consumption, shown as a value and percentage of the total limit. |
| **Max Concurrent Requests** | The highest simultaneous usage observed during the displayed period, such as the last 24 hours. |

The **Usage** indicator uses colors to show the current utilization:

- **Green**: Usage is 50% or below.
- **Amber**: Usage is above 50% and at or below 75%.
- **Red**: Usage is above 75%. Consider increasing the limit to reduce the risk of interrupted requests.

:::note
Realtime **Usage** and **Max Concurrent Requests** can show different values. Usage reflects the current moment, while the maximum records the highest simultaneous demand observed during the stated period.
:::

## Increase a Limit

To add capacity:

1. Find the service you want to increase.
2. Select the `+` control to add one or more packs.
3. Review the updated **Added** and **Total** values.
4. Repeat the selection for any other services that need more capacity.
5. Review the order total at the bottom of the page.
6. Select **Continue**.
7. Confirm the billing details and complete the payment.

Use the `−` control to remove a pack from the pending selection before continuing. The dashboard prevents the selection from exceeding the maximum number of packs available for that service.

After the payment succeeds, the purchased capacity becomes active for the organization.

## Review Pack Charges

The order summary separates the charges into:

- **Current month**: The prorated amount for the time remaining in the current billing month.
- **Next month onwards**: The full recurring monthly amount for the selected packs.

Select or hover over the information icon beside **Total** to review the charge for each selected pack. Applicable taxes are shown separately before payment.

## When a Limit Is Reached

If an organization reaches a concurrency limit, additional requests for that service can fail until an active request ends or more capacity is added.

For example, if all available recording slots are already in use, a request to start another recording is not processed. The number of recordings created earlier in the month does not matter; only recordings active at the same time count toward the concurrent limit.

For limits beyond the maximum available through the Dashboard, [contact VideoSDK](https://www.videosdk.live/contact). Enterprise limits can be configured according to the organization's requirements.

For additional concurrency examples, see [Understanding Usage Quota Limits](../../quotas-and-limit-new.md).

## Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
<summary>Why did a request fail even though my monthly usage is low?</summary>

Usage limits measure simultaneous activity rather than total monthly activity. A request can fail when all concurrent capacity for that service is in use, even if the organization has used the service only briefly during the month.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why is realtime Usage lower than Max Concurrent Requests?</summary>

**Usage** shows activity at the current moment. **Max Concurrent Requests** shows the highest simultaneous activity observed during the stated period, such as the last 24 hours. A previous peak can therefore be higher than current usage.

</details>

<details>
<summary>What should I do if the Dashboard does not offer enough packs?</summary>

The Dashboard limits how many packs can be purchased for each service. Contact VideoSDK to discuss custom or Enterprise capacity when the required limit exceeds the available pack maximum.

</details>

# API Settings & Controls

The VideoSDK Dashboard provides a powerful [API Settings](https://app.videosdk.live/api-keys) section where you can configure various services and controls for your meetings. These settings allow you to customize the behavior of different features directly from the dashboard without requiring code changes.

## Audio/Video Configurations

:::note
Runtime configuration from the dashboard has higher precedence than static SDK configurations.
If a value is modified in the dashboard, it will override any previously defined SDK settings for that session.

Example:
Code: Video = HD → Dashboard: Video = Full HD → Applied: Full HD
:::

### Maximum Send Bitrate Per Participant

Control the maximum total upload bandwidth for all media streams from a single participant.

![Maximum Send Bitrate](https://assets.videosdk.live/images/Screenshot%202026-01-09%20at%2012.00.11%E2%80%AFPM.png)

**Available Options:**
- **Auto**: Removes the upload bitrate limit (recommended for best quality)
- **SD (800kbps)**: Standard definition bitrate
- **HD (1500kbps)**: High definition bitrate
- **Full HD (3000kbps)**: Full high definition bitrate

:::tip
Setting this to **Auto** provides the best video quality as it removes upload bitrate constraints, allowing adaptive streaming based on network conditions.
:::

## Recording & Streaming Configuration

:::note
Recording and HLS follow a precedence-based configuration model:

API/SDK configuration → Highest priority
Dashboard configuration → Used only when no API values are defined

Any parameters explicitly set via the API will not be overridden by dashboard changes.
:::

### Recording Configuration

Configure recording settings for your meetings including layout, quality, and auto-start options.

![Recording Settings](https://assets.videosdk.live/images/Screenshot%202026-01-09%20at%2012.01.00%E2%80%AFPM.png)

**Recording Controls:**
- **Enabled**: Toggle to enable/disable recording functionality
- **Enabled Modes**: Choose between Video & Audio or Audio Only recording
- **Start Recording Automatically**: Auto-start recording when meeting begins
- **Layout Style**: Select Grid layout for recording composition
- **Maximum Tiles In Grid**: Set the number of participants visible in grid (1-25)
- **Who to Prioritize**: Choose Active Speaker or Pinned Participant
- **Theme**: Select System Default, Light, or Dark theme for recordings
- **Video Orientation**: Choose between Landscape or Portrait mode
- **Recording Quality**: Select quality level (e.g., HD Medium)
- **Recording Mode**: Choose between Video & Audio or Audio Only

### HLS Streaming Configuration

Configure HTTP Live Streaming (HLS) settings for broadcasting your meetings.

![HLS Streaming Settings](https://assets.videosdk.live/images/Screenshot%202026-01-09%20at%2012.02.18%E2%80%AFPM.png)

**HLS Streaming Controls:**
- **Enabled**: Toggle to enable/disable HLS streaming
- **Enabled Modes**: Choose between Video & Audio or Audio Only streaming
- **Auto Start HLS**: Automatically start HLS when meeting begins
- **Record HLS Stream**: Enable recording of the HLS stream
- **Layout Style**: Select Grid layout for stream composition
- **Maximum Tiles In Grid**: Set the number of participants visible (1-25)
- **Who to Prioritize**: Choose Active Speaker or Pinned Participant
- **Theme**: Select System Default, Light, or Dark theme
- **HLS Orientation**: Choose between Landscape or Portrait mode
- **HLS Quality**: Select streaming quality (e.g., HD Medium)
- **HLS Streaming Mode**: Choose between Video & Audio or Audio Only

### Additional Service Controls

Enable or disable additional services for your API key.

![Service Controls](https://assets.videosdk.live/images/Screenshot%202026-01-09%20at%2012.03.08%E2%80%AFPM.png)

**Available Services:**
- **RTMP Output**: Enable RTMP streaming to external platforms
- **SIP Integration**: Enable SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) integration for telephony
- **Realtime Translation**: Enable real-time language translation in meetings

### Transcription & Summary

Configure transcription and domain whitelisting for your API key.

![Transcription Settings](https://assets.videosdk.live/images/Screenshot%202026-01-09%20at%2012.03.50%E2%80%AFPM.png)

**Transcription Controls:**
- **Enabled**: Toggle to enable/disable transcription and summary features
- **Whitelist Domain**: Add domain restrictions for API key usage
  - Enter domain names in the format `https://domain.name`
  - Click "Add Domain" to whitelist specific domains
  - Only whitelisted domains can use this API key
  - When no domains are whitelisted, the API key can be used from any domain

# Recording Details

The **Recording Details** page lets you inspect and play the outputs associated with a recording record. The information displayed on the page depends on whether you opened a meeting, participant, track, or composite recording.

To open a recording:

1. Sign in to the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/).
2. Select **RTC** and go to **Recordings**.
3. Open the three-dot menu for a recording.
4. Select **View**.

## Select a Recording Output

The panel on the left lists the recording outputs available for the selected record. Use **Search** to find an output, then select it to update the details and player.

The number beside the page heading and the list label indicates how many outputs are available. Use the copy icon beside an identifier to copy its complete value.

Select the back arrow to return to the Recordings page. Select **Refresh** to retrieve the latest recording information.

## Playback and Actions

When a playable recording is available, use the media player to:

- Play or pause the recording.
- Move backward or forward by 10 seconds.
- Seek to a specific point on the playback timeline.
- Adjust the volume.
- Change the playback speed.
- Enter full-screen mode for supported video recordings.

The recording header can also show its visibility and file size.

- Select **Download** to save the selected recording.
- Select **Delete** to remove the selected recording.

:::warning
Deleting a recording removes that recording output. Confirm that you no longer need it before continuing.
:::

# Recordings

The **Recordings** page lists the recordings created for meeting sessions in your organization. Use it to find a recording, check its processing status and storage destination, and open its detailed view.

![Recordings](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_recordings_table_0545eb08d4.png)

To access the page:

1. Sign in to the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/).
2. Select **RTC**.
3. Select **Recordings** from the navigation sidebar.

## Find and Filter Recordings

Use **Search** to find matching recording records. You can narrow the list further by applying one or more filters.

### Date

Use the **Date** filter to display recordings from the selected date or date range.

### Recording Type

Use the **Recording Type** filter to select one or more recording types:

- **Meeting Recording**
- **Participant Recording**
- **Track Recording**
- **Composite Recording**

### Cloud Storage

Use the **Cloud Storage** filter to find recordings by storage destination:

- **VideoSDK**
- **GCP**
- **Azure**
- **AWS**
- **Presigned URL**

### Transcription

Use the **Transcription** filter to display recordings based on whether transcription is:

- **Available**
- **Not Available**

### Status

Use the **Status** filter to select one or more recording states:

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Saved** | The recording was processed and saved successfully. |
| **In Progress** | The recording is still being processed. |
| **Failed** | The recording could not be completed or saved. |

Select the required options in a filter and then select **Apply**. When multiple filters are active, the recordings list must match the selected filter criteria.

## Recordings Table

Each row represents a recording record associated with a meeting session.

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Meeting Id** | The unique ID of the meeting associated with the recording. |
| **Session Id** | The unique ID of the meeting session in which the recording was created. |
| **Date** | The date and time associated with the recording. |
| **Recording Type** | The type of recording, such as meeting, participant, track, or composite recording. |
| **Storage** | The storage destination used for the recording. |
| **Transcription** | Indicates whether a transcription is available for the recording. |
| **Status** | The current processing or storage state of the recording. |
| **Actions** | Provides the actions available for the recording. |

If an ID is shortened in the table, hover over it to view the complete value.

## Open a Recording

Select the three-dot menu in the **Actions** column, then select **View** to open the recording.

The information and actions in the detailed view vary by recording type. See [Recording Details](./recordings/recording-details) for the type-specific fields.

## Refresh the Recordings List

Select **Refresh** to retrieve the latest recording data. This is useful for recordings whose status is still **In Progress**.

## Navigate the Recordings List

Use the controls below the table to:

- Move to the previous or next page.
- Select a specific page.
- Change the number of recording records displayed per page.

The counter at the bottom of the table shows the number of displayed records and the total number of available records.

:::note
The recording types, storage information, transcription availability, statuses, and actions shown depend on how each recording was configured and processed.
:::

# Errors

The **Errors** tab lists errors recorded during a meeting session. Use it to identify affected participants, understand failed or invalid operations, and gather context for troubleshooting.

![Session errors](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_sessions_error_08ef8b0974.png)

To open the tab:

1. Sign in to the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/).
2. Select **RTC** and go to **Sessions**.
3. Open a session record.
4. Select **Errors**.

## Errors Table

Each row represents an error occurrence recorded during the session.

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Participant Name** | The display name and participant ID associated with the error. |
| **Error details** | Information about the operation that produced the error, the reported error message, and an explanation when available. |

The same participant can appear in multiple rows when more than one error was recorded. Repeated error messages indicate that the same type of error occurred more than once.

## Interpret an Error

An error entry can provide:

- The SDK method, operation, or session activity associated with the error.
- A short description of the reported problem.
- Additional context about why the operation could not be completed.
- The participant associated with the occurrence.

For example, an error can indicate that an application attempted to perform a media action that was not valid for the participant's current state. The exact errors and details shown depend on the SDK and the activity recorded during the session.

## Troubleshoot Session Errors

Use the information in an error entry to identify the affected operation and participant. You can then:

1. Open [Participant Details](./participant-details) to review the participant's environment, timeline, and media-quality data.
2. Open [Traces](./traces) to inspect the operations and state changes recorded around the issue.
3. Check the application logic associated with the reported SDK method or operation.
4. Compare repeated occurrences to determine whether the issue affected one participant or appeared across multiple clients.

## Error Availability

Session errors are available only when they are supported and reported by the SDK version used by the participant. The dashboard displays the applicable minimum SDK-version requirements on the Errors tab.

If no errors are displayed, it can mean:

- No supported errors were recorded during the session.
- The participant used an SDK or SDK version that does not provide this error data.
- The required diagnostic data was not available for the session.

:::note
The Errors tab contains the errors reported to VideoSDK for the session. Its contents can vary by SDK, SDK version, platform, application behavior, and the diagnostic data collected.
:::

# Participant Details

The **Participant Details** page provides connection, device, timeline, and media-quality information for an individual participant. Use it to investigate a participant's experience during a meeting session.

![Session Participant Details](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_sessions_participant_view_38512e8796.png)

## Open Participant Details

From the [Session Overview](./session-overview), open a participant using either of these methods:

- In the graphical timeline, select **View Details** for the participant.
- In the participant table, select the arrow at the end of the participant's row.

Select **Go back to participant list** to return to the Session Overview.

## Participant Summary

The page header identifies the meeting, its duration, and the selected participant. The participant summary provides the following information when available:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Participant ID** | The unique ID assigned to the participant. |
| **Participant name** | The participant's display name. |
| **Total Duration** | The total time the participant remained in the session. |
| **Mode** | The participant's meeting mode. |
| **Joined at** | The date and time when the participant joined the session. |
| **Left at** | The date and time when the participant left the session. |
| **Joining time** | The time taken by the participant to join the session. |
| **multiStream** | The multistream value recorded for the participant. |
| **Location** | The participant's approximate geographic location. |
| **Platform** | The type of platform used, such as desktop. |
| **Device Info** | Information reported for the participant's device. |
| **OS** | The operating system used by the participant. |
| **Browser** | The browser used by the participant. |
| **SDK Version** | The VideoSDK package and version used by the participant. |

Use the copy icon beside the participant ID to copy its value.

## Participant's Timeline

The participant timeline places the participant's activity on the overall session time scale.

- **Overall Session Timeline** shows when the participant joined and left the session.
- **Audio Timeline** shows when the participant's microphone or audio stream started and stopped.
- **Video Timeline** shows when the participant's webcam or video stream started and stopped.

Hover over an event icon to view the event and its exact timestamp. The available timelines and indicators depend on the streams used and events recorded for the participant. For example, the video timeline can be empty or unavailable when the participant did not enable the webcam or joined an audio-only session.

## Participant Call Health

The **Participant Call Health** section provides a quick view of the participant's media quality over time. Select **Audio** or **Video** to view the corresponding media type.

![Session Participant Call Health](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/dashboard_sessions_participant_call_health_ed44a41fa2.png)

Hover over an interval to view the timestamp and its average:

- Jitter
- Round-trip time (RTT)
- Packet-loss percentage

Use this section to identify when the participant's connection quality changed during the session.

## Participant Session Stats

Expand **Participant Session Stats** to inspect detailed media and device metrics. Select a media tab, then choose a **Receiver Participant** to compare the selected sender and receiver data.

<!-- IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Add a screenshot of Participant Session Stats here. -->

The graphs place metric values on a session timeline. You can:

- Hover over a graph point to view its timestamp and exact value.
- Drag the handles below a graph to focus on a specific time range.
- Use the expand icon, when available, to enlarge a graph.
- Select **Hide Session Stats** to collapse the section.

The dashboard displays sender and receiver graphs side by side when data is available.

### Stats by Media Type

defaultValue="audio"
groupId={"participant-stats-media"}
