# IoT SDK + AI Agent Example

You can pair the IoT SDK with a VideoSDK AI Agent so a device joins the same room as the agent. The device streams its audio to the agent, and the agent listens, processes the audio, and responds in real time. This gives the device two-way voice interaction.

#### What You Can Build

###### Smart Home & Lifestyle

- **Adaptive Climate Control**: a thermostat that reports the temperature and takes spoken instructions to adjust it.

- **Interactive Home Chef**: a kitchen device that suggests recipes and guides the user through them by voice.

- **Wellness Coach**: a wearable that monitors heart rate and gives spoken prompts, such as a breathing exercise when the rate spikes.

###### Education & Entertainment

- **Child-Friendly Storyteller**: a toy that reads stories aloud, changes character voices, and answers a child's questions.

- **Interactive Tutor**: a classroom device that answers students' questions aloud and adjusts its explanations to each student.

Any device that can join a room alongside an AI Agent can support similar two-way voice use cases.

#### Demo: IoT SDK in Conversation with AI Agent
<div style={{textAlign: 'center'}}>

<ReactPlayer controls url='https://cdn.videosdk.live/docs/iotsdk/iot_ai_agent_demo.mp4' height="560px" width={"100%"}/>

</div>
---

### Prerequisites
Before you get started, ensure you have the following:

- **Python**: Python version >= 3.11, for the AI Agent side
- Video SDK Developer Account (Not having one, follow **[Video SDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/)**)
---

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 1: Setup for AI Agent
</div>
<Step number={1} title="Setup for AI Agent">
On the AI Agent side, configure it to join the room as a participant. It listens to the device's audio, processes it, and generates responses in real time, handling speech recognition, reasoning, and synthesis for low-latency two-way interaction between the device and the room.

```python
def make_context() -> JobContext:
    room_options = RoomOptions(
        room_id="YOUR_ROOM_ID",
        name="VideoSDK Cascaded Agent",
        playground=True
    )

    return JobContext(room_options=room_options)
```

:::caution 
Make sure you keep the **same room ID in the RoomOptions** here, which you’ll also use on the IoT device side later.
:::


<div style={{fontWeight: 'bold', fontSize: '18px', marginTop: '20px'}}>
See the full setup in the <a href="https://docs.videosdk.live/ai_agents/voice-agent-quick-start">AI Agent Quick Start Guide</a>
</div>

</Step>

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 2: Setup for IoT SDK
</div>
<Step number={2} title="Setup IoT SDK">

Now it’s time to configure the `IoT SDK` on your ESP device. This step enables the device to `capture` and `publish` audio streams into the room, as well as `receive` and `play` responses from the `AI Agent`. With this setup, your device transitions from being a `simple` endpoint to an `active` communication node.

```c
// Token and room ID come from menuconfig -> "VideoSDK Configuration",
// so no real token has to sit in source.
char *token = CONFIG_VIDEOSDK_TOKEN;

init_config_t init_cfg = {
    .roomId = CONFIG_VIDEOSDK_ROOM_ID,  // same room as the agent
    .token = token,
    .displayName = "ESP32-Device",
    .participantId = "your participant id",   // "" or NULL => a random id is generated
    .audioCodec = AUDIO_CODEC_OPUS,
    .videoCodec = VIDEO_CODEC_NONE,           // audio-only agent
};

result_t init_result = init(&init_cfg);
printf("Result: %d\n", init_result);

```

:::caution 
Ensure that the room ID configured on the IoT device is identical to the room ID defined in the AI Agent’s `RoomOptions`.
:::


<div style={{fontWeight: 'bold', fontSize: '18px', marginTop: '20px'}}>
See the full setup in the <a href="/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/quickstart/quick-start">IoT SDK Quick Start Guide</a>
</div>

</Step>

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 3: Connect the IoT Device and AI Agent
</div>
<Step number={3} title="Connect the IoT Device and AI Agent">

Run the two sides together:

1. The AI Agent joins the room first.

```python
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Start the AI Agent, which will join the room as a participant
    job = WorkerJob(entrypoint=start_session, jobctx=make_context) 
    #highlight-start
    job.start()
    #highlight-end
```
2. The IoT device then joins the same room and starts publishing and subscribing to audio.

```c
  // joining the User through IoT - device once AI - Agent joins the room.
  // highlight-start
  result_t result_publish = startPublishAudio(); 
  result_t result_subscribe = startSubscribeAudio();
  //highlight-end
  printf("Result Publish:%d\n", result_publish);
  printf("Result Subscribe:%d\n", result_subscribe); 
```  

:::note Supported hardware
Two-way voice needs a board with a speaker so the device can play the agent's replies. Without one, [`startSubscribeAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startsubscribeaudio) returns `DEVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED`, so the device can send audio to the agent but cannot play its replies. Refer [Supported Microcontrollers](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/supported-browser-and-device-os).
:::

3. The device and the AI Agent now exchange audio in both directions in real time.

</Step>

# IoT Quick Start

 The IoT SDK enables real-time audio and video conferencing by connecting devices directly to the VideoSDK server. Devices can join rooms, publish audio and video or sensor data, and subscribe to other participants' streams.

## Prerequisites

Before you get started, ensure you have the following:

- **ESP-IDF**: ESP-IDF versions **v5.4.2, v5.4.3, or v5.4.4**
- **Python**: Python version >= **v3.11**
- A supported **ESP32-S3** board. For a list of supported boards, see [Supported Microcontrollers](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/supported-browser-and-device-os).
- Video SDK Developer Account (Not having one, follow **[Video SDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/)**)

## Install VideoSDK's IoT component

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 1: Setup for esp-idf
</div>
<Step number={1} title="Setup for esp-idf">
Install and configure the ESP-IDF environment on your system to prepare the toolchain, dependencies, and base project structure for development.
For more information visit [**ESP-IDF**](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32/get-started/index.html)

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 2: Add IoT SDK component
</div>
<Step number={2} title="Add IoT SDK component">
The IoT SDK is published on the [ESP Component Registry](https://components.espressif.com/components/videosdk/iot-sdk) as `videosdk/iot-sdk`. Create a file named `idf_component.yml` in your `main` folder and add it as a managed dependency. ESP-IDF downloads it on the next build, so there is nothing to clone.

```yml title="main/idf_component.yml"
dependencies:
  videosdk/iot-sdk: '*'
  idf:
    version: ">=5.4.2,<=5.4.4"
  mdns: "*"
  # Wi-Fi/network helper (example_connect). Bundled with ESP-IDF,
  # resolved from $IDF_PATH, not a registry component.
  protocol_examples_common:
    path: ${IDF_PATH}/examples/common_components/protocol_examples_common
```

</Step>

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 3: Update your CmakeLists.txt
</div>
<Step number={3} title="Update your CmakeLists.txt">
This ensures that your project links correctly with the required IoT SDK and ESP-IDF components. Replace `your-project-name.c` with the name of your source file.
For more information visit [**CMake**](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/)

```cmake title="main/CMakeLists.txt"
idf_component_register(
    SRCS "your-project-name.c"
    INCLUDE_DIRS "."
    REQUIRES mbedtls json esp_netif fatfs vfs esp_common esp_timer esp_lcd nvs_flash
)

# libsrtp pointer-type mismatch on Xtensa with ESP-IDF 5.4.2+: uint32_t is
# 'long unsigned int' there, while srtp.c uses 'unsigned int'. Same width,
# but the compiler treats the pointers as incompatible.
idf_component_get_property(srtp_lib sepfy__srtp COMPONENT_LIB)
target_compile_options(${srtp_lib} PRIVATE -Wno-incompatible-pointer-types)

target_compile_options(${COMPONENT_LIB} PRIVATE "-Wno-format")
```

:::warning
The two `target_compile_options` lines are required. Without the libsrtp option the project **fails to build** on ESP-IDF 5.4.2+.
:::
</Step>

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 4: Create Partitions Table
</div>
<Step number={4} title="Create Partitions Table">
Create a file named `partitions.csv` in your project folder. This file defines the flash memory layout for your device. The same layout is used on both supported boards.
For more information visit [**Partitions Table**](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/stable/esp32/api-guides/partition-tables.html)

```csv title="partitions.csv"
# ESP-IDF Partition Table
# Name,   Type, SubType, Offset,  Size, Flags
nvs,      data, nvs,     0x9000,  0x6000,
phy_init, data, phy,     0xf000,  0x1000,
factory,  app,  factory, 0x10000, 4M,
```

</Step>

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 5: Add board configurations
</div>
<Step number={5} title="Add board configurations">

Create a file named `sdkconfig.defaults` in your project folder. These values are tuned so the SDK has enough memory and CPU. The SDK runs audio, video and the network stack at the same time on the ESP32-S3.
For more information [**sdkconfig**](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32/api-reference/kconfig-reference.html)

```bash title="sdkconfig.defaults"
# Pick your board first, under menuconfig -> "SET Microcontroller"
# (ESP32-S3-Korvo-2 or the XIAO ESP32-S3)
CONFIG_IDF_TARGET="esp32s3"
CONFIG_APP_RETRIEVE_LEN_ELF_SHA=16

# Flash: this board has 8 MB, and QIO (4-line) reads run code from flash roughly
# twice as fast as the default 2-line mode. A custom partition table is used to
# fit the app.
CONFIG_ESPTOOLPY_FLASHSIZE_8MB=y
CONFIG_ESPTOOLPY_FLASHSIZE="8MB"
CONFIG_ESPTOOLPY_FLASHMODE_QIO=y
CONFIG_PARTITION_TABLE_CUSTOM=y

CONFIG_EXAMPLE_CONNECT_IPV6=n
CONFIG_ESP_PHY_REDUCE_TX_POWER=y

# PSRAM (external RAM), REQUIRED. The SDK's audio/video buffers and the WiFi
# network buffers live here so the small, fast internal RAM stays free for
# time-critical work. Running PSRAM at 80 MHz roughly doubles its bandwidth,
# which speeds up the whole audio + video + network path.
CONFIG_SPIRAM=y
CONFIG_SPIRAM_MODE_OCT=y
CONFIG_SPIRAM_SPEED_80M=y
CONFIG_SPIRAM_USE_MALLOC=y

# Keep WiFi/network buffers and task stacks in PSRAM so enough internal RAM stays
# free while a call is active. Without these, the device can fail to connect or
# reset once audio and video are both streaming.
CONFIG_SPIRAM_TRY_ALLOCATE_WIFI_LWIP=y
CONFIG_SPIRAM_ALLOW_STACK_EXTERNAL_MEMORY=y

# Reserve a slice of fast internal RAM for the WiFi driver and encryption, which
# cannot run from PSRAM. This is what keeps outgoing audio/video packets flowing
# when the network is busy. Do not lower these; raising the reserve does not help
# if you are short on RAM, reduce what you allocate instead.
CONFIG_SPIRAM_MALLOC_ALWAYSINTERNAL=1024
CONFIG_SPIRAM_MALLOC_RESERVE_INTERNAL=16384

# Run at full 240 MHz and build size-optimized (-Os). -Os is noticeably faster
# than the debug default for the SDK's audio/video/network code, not just smaller.
CONFIG_ESP_DEFAULT_CPU_FREQ_MHZ_240=y
CONFIG_COMPILER_OPTIMIZATION_SIZE=y

# 1 ms scheduler tick: smoother time-sharing between the audio, video, and
# network tasks, which reduces jitter in the call.
CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000

# Task stacks sized for the SDK's signaling and media work.
CONFIG_ESP_SYSTEM_EVENT_TASK_STACK_SIZE=3072
CONFIG_ESP_MAIN_TASK_STACK_SIZE=10240
CONFIG_ESP_TASK_WDT_CHECK_IDLE_TASK_CPU1=n
CONFIG_ESP_IPC_TASK_STACK_SIZE=2048

# WiFi + TCP/IP buffers tuned so the video stream does not starve the network
# stack and drop outgoing packets.
CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_STATIC_RX_BUFFER_NUM=16
CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_DYNAMIC_RX_BUFFER_NUM=48
CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_DYNAMIC_TX_BUFFER_NUM=32
CONFIG_LWIP_IPV6_AUTOCONFIG=y
CONFIG_LWIP_IPV6_DHCP6=y
CONFIG_LWIP_TCP_SND_BUF_DEFAULT=5744
CONFIG_LWIP_TCP_WND_DEFAULT=5744
# Larger inbound UDP queue so received audio/video is not dropped while the
# outgoing stream keeps the network busy.
CONFIG_LWIP_UDP_RECVMBOX_SIZE=64

# Logging. A normal build is quiet, lifecycle messages, warnings, and errors
# only. This line compiles the SDK's debug logs into the image (a few KB of
# flash) WITHOUT turning them on, so you can enable them later at
# menuconfig -> "VideoSDK Logging" -> Debug, or from code with
# videosdk_set_log_mode(VIDEOSDK_LOG_DEBUG). Leave it in, or debug mode prints
# nothing extra.
CONFIG_LOG_MAXIMUM_LEVEL_DEBUG=y

# TLS / DTLS, required to reach the VideoSDK signaling server over wss:// and
# for the encrypted WebRTC media transport. The certificate bundle verifies the
# server's certificate.
CONFIG_MBEDTLS_EXTERNAL_MEM_ALLOC=y
CONFIG_MBEDTLS_SSL_PROTO_DTLS=y
CONFIG_MBEDTLS_CERTIFICATE_BUNDLE=y
CONFIG_MBEDTLS_CERTIFICATE_BUNDLE_DEFAULT_FULL=y
CONFIG_PTHREAD_TASK_STACK_SIZE_DEFAULT=8192

# Camera (used by the video send path). The common sensors are enabled so the
# driver auto-detects whichever one is fitted on your board.
CONFIG_OV2640_SUPPORT=y
CONFIG_OV3660_SUPPORT=y
CONFIG_OV5640_SUPPORT=y
CONFIG_CAMERA_DMA_BUFFER_SIZE_MAX=32768
```

:::warning
`sdkconfig.defaults` is read only on the first build, when no `sdkconfig` file exists yet. If you have already built the project once, delete the generated `sdkconfig` before rebuilding; otherwise these values are silently ignored.
:::
</Step>

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 6: Update your-project-main.c
</div>
<Step number={6} title="Update your-project-main.c">

Write your project logic inside `your-project-name.c`. This is where you initialize the IoT SDK, join the room, and start streaming.

The token and room ID are read from `menuconfig` (Step 7)
```c title="main/your-project-name.c"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "esp_event.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
#include "esp_mac.h"
#include "esp_netif.h"
#include "esp_system.h"
#include "freertos/FreeRTOS.h"
#include "freertos/task.h"   // vTaskDelay, pdMS_TO_TICKS
#include "mdns.h"
#include "nvs_flash.h"
#include "protocol_examples_common.h"
#include "sdkconfig.h"
#include "videosdk.h"

static const char *TAG = "IOT-SDK";

// Set your token under menuconfig -> "VideoSDK Configuration".
// Not const: init_config_t.token is a char*. The SDK copies what you pass, so
// this buffer is not retained after init() returns.
char *token = CONFIG_VIDEOSDK_TOKEN;

void app_main(void)
{
    static char deviceid[32] = {0};
    uint8_t mac[8] = {0};

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "[APP] Startup..");
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "[APP] IDF version: %s", esp_get_idf_version());

    // Log verbosity, chosen in menuconfig -> "VideoSDK Logging".
    // Call it before init() so it covers the join.
#if CONFIG_VIDEOSDK_LOG_MODE_DEBUG
    videosdk_set_log_mode(VIDEOSDK_LOG_DEBUG);
#else
    videosdk_set_log_mode(VIDEOSDK_LOG_NORMAL);
#endif

    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(nvs_flash_init());
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_netif_init());
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_event_loop_create_default());
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(example_connect());

    // A stable participant id derived from this board's Wi-Fi MAC.
    if (esp_read_mac(mac, ESP_MAC_WIFI_STA) == ESP_OK) {
        sprintf(deviceid, "esp32-%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x",
                mac[0], mac[1], mac[2], mac[3], mac[4], mac[5]);
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Device ID: %s", deviceid);
    }

    if (token[0] == '\0' || CONFIG_VIDEOSDK_ROOM_ID[0] == '\0') {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Token / room ID not set. Run 'idf.py menuconfig'"
                      " -> VideoSDK Configuration.");
        return;
    }

    init_config_t init_cfg = {
        .roomId        = CONFIG_VIDEOSDK_ROOM_ID,
        .token         = token,
        .displayName   = "ESP32S3-Device",   // shown to other participants
        .participantId = deviceid,           
        .audioCodec    = AUDIO_CODEC_PCMA,   // PCMA, PCMU or OPUS
        .videoCodec    = VIDEO_CODEC_JPEG,   // VIDEO_CODEC_NONE for audio-only
    };

    result_t init_result = init(&init_cfg);
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "init: %d", init_result);
    if (init_result != RESULT_OK) {
        return;
    }

    // Send the microphone and the camera into the room.
    // Both supported boards can publish.
    result_t publish_audio = startPublishAudio();
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "startPublishAudio: %d", publish_audio);

    result_t publish_video = startPublishVideo();
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "startPublishVideo: %d", publish_video);

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // RECEIVING (playing remote audio / showing remote video).
    //
    // Needs a board with a speaker and a display; on boards without them the
    // subscribe calls return DEVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED (3004). See the
    // Supported Microcontrollers page for board capabilities.
    //
    // To use them, select the Korvo-2 under
    //   menuconfig -> "SET Microcontroller" -> "Audio hardware board"
    // and uncomment:
    //
    // result_t subscribe_audio = startSubscribeAudio();
    // ESP_LOGI(TAG, "startSubscribeAudio: %d", subscribe_audio);
    //
    // result_t subscribe_video = startSubscribeVideo();
    // ESP_LOGI(TAG, "startSubscribeVideo: %d", subscribe_video);
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    // Keep the session active for a defined duration (adjust as per your application use case)
    // vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(100000));

    // leave() stops every stream that was started.
    // result_t result_leave = leave();
    // ESP_LOGI(TAG, "leave: %d", result_leave);

    // Keep main loop alive
    while (1) {
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));
    }
}
```
</Step>

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 7: Configure the project
</div>
<Step number={7} title="Configure the project">

Set your board as the build target, then open `menuconfig` to set your Wi-Fi, token, room ID, and board.


```bash
# Set your board as the target
idf.py set-target esp32s3

# Open the configuration menu
idf.py menuconfig
```

Inside `menuconfig`, set the following. Press `S` to save and `Enter` to confirm, then `Esc` or `q` to exit.

```
a. Example Connection Configuration
       |-> WIFI SSID              <!-- your WiFi name -->
       |-> WIFI Password          <!-- your WiFi password -->

b. VideoSDK Configuration
       |-> Auth token (JWT)       <!-- paste your VideoSDK token -->
       |-> Room ID                <!-- the room you want to join -->

c. SET Microcontroller
       |-> Audio hardware board
             |-> ESP32-S3-XIAO      (default)
             |-> ESP32-S3-Korvo-2
       |-> Speaker output volume (0-100)   <!-- board-dependent; see Supported Microcontrollers -->

d. VideoSDK Logging
       |-> Log verbosity
             |-> Normal (default)
             |-> Debug

e. Partition table                   <!-- already set by sdkconfig.defaults -->
       |-> Custom partition table CSV

f. Serial flasher config             <!-- already set by sdkconfig.defaults -->
       |-> Flash size: 8 MB
```

</Step>

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 8: Build & Flash Project
</div>
<Step number={8} title="Build & Flash Project">

Build the firmware and flash it onto your board.

```bash
# Build the project
idf.py build

# Flash it to your board and open the monitor
idf.py flash monitor
```

`idf.py flash monitor` auto-detects the serial port when a single board is connected, so you usually do not need to specify one. Exit the monitor with `Ctrl+]`. On Linux, add yourself to the `dialout` group first (`sudo usermod -a -G dialout $USER`, then log out and back in) or the flash step fails with a permission error.

:::note More than one device connected?
If you have several USB-serial devices plugged in, auto-detect cannot tell which is your board. Pass the port explicitly with `idf.py -p <PORT> flash monitor`. Find `<PORT>` by listing the ports before and after plugging the board in; the entry that appears is your port.

| OS | Command | Typical value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS | `ls /dev/cu.*` | `/dev/cu.usbmodem*` or `/dev/cu.usbserial-*` |
| Linux | `ls /dev/ttyUSB* /dev/ttyACM*` | `/dev/ttyUSB0` or `/dev/ttyACM0` |
| Windows | `mode` or Device Manager -> Ports (COM & LPT) | `COM3` |
:::

</Step>

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 9: Connecting with VideoSDK Client Applications
</div>
<Step number={9} title="Connecting with VideoSDK Client Applications">
Integrate IoT devices with VideoSDK client applications. Ensure that both the IoT device and client apps connect to the same room for communication.


<div className="heading-toc-only">
</div>

<!-- When working with a Client SDK, make sure to create the room first using the [Create Room API](https://docs.videosdk.live/api-reference/realtime-communication/create-room)
. Then, simply pass the generated `room id` in both your client SDK and the `RoomOptions` for your AI Agent so they connect to the same session. -->

<AllSDKCard showText={true}/>
</Step>

:::tip
You can checkout the complete [quick start example here](https://github.com/videosdk-live/videosdk-rtc-iot-sdk-example).
:::

:::tip
Prefer a ready-made project? The component ships two runnable examples you can scaffold in one command:

```bash
idf.py create-project-from-example "videosdk/iot-sdk=0.4.0:audio_call"
idf.py create-project-from-example "videosdk/iot-sdk=0.4.0:video_call"
```
:::

## Next steps

Your device is in a room. What to build on top of it:

- **Keep it there.** A device on Wi-Fi will lose its session eventually. [Connection State](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/connection-state) shows how to detect the drop and rejoin.
- **Audio**: [Publish Audio](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/handling-audio/publish-audio) · [Subscribe Audio](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/handling-audio/subscribe-audio)
- **Video**: [Publish Video](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/handling-video/publish-video) · [Subscribe Video](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/handling-video/subscribe-video)
- **Data Channel**: send commands, sensor readings and status updates alongside the media. [Send Message](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/data-channel/send-message) · [Receive Message](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/data-channel/receive-message)
- **Talk to an AI agent**: [IoT + AI Agent](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/quickstart/iot-ai-agent) pairs the device with a VideoSDK AI Agent for two-way voice, with no model running on the device.
- **When something fails**: every call returns a [result code](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/result-code), and [Logging and Debugging](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/logging-and-debugging) covers turning on the SDK's debug logs and reading the monitor.
- **Leave cleanly**: [Leave Room](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/leave-room) tears down every stream the session started.

# Run a Sample IoT SDK Project

The IoT SDK ships two ready-to-run sample projects inside the published component on the [ESP Component Registry](https://components.espressif.com/components/videosdk/iot-sdk):

| Example | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `audio_call` | Joins a room and streams audio. |
| `video_call` | Joins a room and streams video. |

`idf.py create-project-from-example` downloads the component and scaffolds the whole project for you: source, `CMakeLists.txt`, `partitions.csv` and a tuned `sdkconfig.defaults`. There is nothing to wire up by hand.

The same samples are also available on GitHub: [videosdk-rtc-iot-sdk-example](https://github.com/videosdk-live/videosdk-rtc-iot-sdk-example).

:::tip
If you would rather build a project from scratch and add the SDK to it yourself, follow the [Quick Start](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/quickstart/quick-start) instead.
:::

## Prerequisites

Before you get started, ensure you have the following:

- **ESP-IDF**: ESP-IDF **v5.4.2, v5.4.3, or v5.4.4**
- **Python**: Python version >= 3.11
- A supported **ESP32-S3** board. For a list of supported boards, see [Supported Microcontrollers](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/supported-browser-and-device-os).
- A valid [Video SDK Account](https://app.videosdk.live/)

### Generate Token

To manage secured communication, every participant that connects to a room needs an access token. You can easily generate this token from the [VideoSDK Dashboard](https://app.videosdk.live/api-keys).

**For development purpose**, you can generate a temporary token from [VideoSDK Dashboard's API section](https://app.videosdk.live/api-keys).

import ReactPlayer from "react-player";

  autoplay
  muted

  url="/video/dashboard_token_generation.mp4"
  width={"100%"}

/>

## Run the Sample Project

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 1: Configure the ESP-IDF environment
</div>
<Step number={1} title="Configure the ESP-IDF environment">
:::tip
For setting up **ESP-IDF**, follow only **Step 1** of the [Quick Start](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/quickstart/quick-start).
Inside that step, you do not need to run the project creation commands; the next step here creates the project for you.
:::

Once the toolchain is installed, activate it in your shell:

```bash
source ~/esp/esp-idf/export.sh
```
</Step>

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 2: Create the sample project
</div>
<Step number={2} title="Create the sample project">

Pick the example you want and run one command. It fetches the component from the registry and generates a complete project in the current directory.

```bash
# Audio call
idf.py create-project-from-example "videosdk/iot-sdk=0.4.0:audio_call"

# ...or video call
idf.py create-project-from-example "videosdk/iot-sdk=0.4.0:video_call"
```

Then move into the generated folder:

```bash
cd audio_call     # or: cd video_call
```

:::note
The generated project already contains everything the SDK needs: `main/idf_component.yml`, `main/CMakeLists.txt`, `partitions.csv` and a tuned `sdkconfig.defaults`. The board, token, room ID and log-verbosity menus come from the component itself, so there is no `Kconfig.projbuild` to write.
:::
</Step>

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 3: Configure your board and credentials
</div>
<Step number={3} title="Configure your board and credentials">

Set the target, then set your Wi-Fi, token and room ID in `menuconfig`.


```bash
idf.py set-target esp32s3
idf.py menuconfig
```

Inside `menuconfig`, set the following. Press `S` to save and `Enter` to confirm, then `Esc` or `q` to exit.

```
a. Example Connection Configuration
       |-> WIFI SSID              <!-- your WiFi name -->
       |-> WIFI Password          <!-- your WiFi password -->

b. VideoSDK Configuration
       |-> Auth token (JWT)       <!-- paste your VideoSDK token -->
       |-> Room ID                <!-- the room you want to join -->

c. SET Microcontroller
       |-> Audio hardware board
             |-> ESP32-S3-XIAO      (default)
             |-> ESP32-S3-Korvo-2
       |-> Speaker output volume (0-100)   <!-- board-dependent; see Supported Microcontrollers -->

d. VideoSDK Logging
       |-> Log verbosity
             |-> Normal (default)
             |-> Debug
```

The token and room ID live in `sdkconfig`, not in source, so you never have to paste a real token into a `.c` file.

:::note Sending vs receiving
All boards can send audio and video. Receiving needs a speaker and a display; on boards without them, `startSubscribeAudio()` and `startSubscribeVideo()` return `DEVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED` (expected, not a failure). See [Supported Microcontrollers](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/supported-browser-and-device-os).
:::
</Step>

<div className="heading-toc-only">
### Step 4: Build & Flash Project
</div>
<Step number={4} title="Build & Flash Project">

Build the firmware and flash it onto your board.

```bash
idf.py build
idf.py flash monitor
```

`idf.py flash monitor` auto-detects the serial port when a single board is connected, so you usually do not need to specify one. Exit the monitor with `Ctrl+]`. On Linux, add yourself to the `dialout` group first (`sudo usermod -a -G dialout $USER`, then log out and back in) or flashing fails with a permission error.

:::note More than one device connected?
If you have several USB-serial devices plugged in, auto-detect cannot tell which is your board. Pass the port explicitly with `idf.py -p <PORT> flash monitor`, where `<PORT>` is `/dev/cu.usbmodem*` or `/dev/cu.usbserial-*` on macOS (`ls /dev/cu.*`), `/dev/ttyUSB*` or `/dev/ttyACM*` on Linux, or `COMx` on Windows (Device Manager -> Ports). List the ports before and after plugging the board in; the entry that appears is your port.
:::


You can checkout the complete [quick start example here](https://github.com/videosdk-live/videosdk-rtc-iot-sdk-example).



Join the same room ID from a browser or a phone using any [VideoSDK client SDK](https://docs.videosdk.live/), and the device will appear as another participant.

</Step>

# Release Notes - IoT

This page will keep you updated with all the releases of IoT SDK.


## v0.4.0

**Release Date** : 7th August 2026

The SDK now uses "room" terminology throughout, matching the VideoSDK signaling API.

#### Breaking Changes

- `init_config_t.meetingID` is now [`roomId`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init). Same value, new name.
- `create_meeting()` is now [`create_room()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#create_room), returning `create_room_result_t`. Arguments and the returned `room_id` are unchanged.
- The menuconfig option `VIDEOSDK_MEETING_ID` is now `VIDEOSDK_ROOM_ID` (`CONFIG_VIDEOSDK_ROOM_ID` in your code). Re-enter the ID in `idf.py menuconfig` after upgrading.

#### Features

- Per-stream stop and restart without leaving the room: [`stopPublishAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#stoppublishaudio), [`stopPublishVideo()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#stoppublishvideo), [`stopSubscribeAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#stopsubscribeaudio) and [`stopSubscribeVideo()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#stopsubscribevideo). The matching `start*` brings a stream back, and the calls are safe when the stream is not running. [`leave()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#leave) is unchanged.
- New `init_config_t.signalingBaseUrl` points the SDK at a different VideoSDK API host. Leave it `NULL` for the default.

#### Improvements

- The **Debug** log mode now includes video-receive diagnostics.

---

## v0.3.2

**Release Date** : 31st July 2026

#### Documentation

- Docs & reliability: Reorganized and refreshed the guides (boards-as-rows tables with hardware links, clearer prerequisites, up-to-date version pins), plus more detailed connection error reporting and steadier data-channel handling in the refreshed prebuilt libraries.

---

## v0.3.1

**Release Date** : 27th July 2026

#### Breaking Changes

- The separate stop-audio calls were removed. The SDK now tears down every direction automatically when you call [`leave()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#leave), so `stopPublishAudio()` and `stopSubscribeAudio()` are no longer available.
- The `DUPLICATE_ID` (3024) result code was removed. All other result codes remain unchanged.

#### Improvements

- More dependable video reception on the ESP32-S3-Korvo-2, with smoother display playback.

#### Updates

- Tested and supported on ESP-IDF 5.4.2, 5.4.3, and 5.4.4.

---

## v0.3.0

**Release Date** : 11th July 2026

#### Breaking Changes

- [`startPublishAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startpublishaudio) no longer takes an argument. Set the device's id once in the new `init_config_t.participantId` field instead:

```c
// before
startPublishAudio("my-device-id");

// now
init_config_t cfg = { ..., .participantId = "my-device-id" };
init(&cfg);
startPublishAudio();
```

  Leave `participantId` as `""` or `NULL` and you still get a random id, as before.

- `init_config_t` has a new `participantId` field. Rebuild your application against the new header. See [Initialize Room](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/init-room).

#### Features

- **Send and receive messages during a call.** Open the channel with [`startMessageChannel()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startmessagechannel), send text or binary with [`sendMessage()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#sendmessage), and close it with [`stopMessageChannel()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#stopmessagechannel). Register [`setDataMessageHandler()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#setdatamessagehandler) to receive what other participants send. See [Send Message](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/data-channel/send-message) and [Receive Message](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/data-channel/receive-message).
- [`setConnectionStateHandler()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#setconnectionstatehandler) reports when the connection comes up or drops, so your application can rejoin after a disconnect.
- Audio can be sent as **PCMU** or **Opus** in addition to **PCMA**. Pick one with `init_config_t.audioCodec`.
- Pick the log verbosity at runtime with `videosdk_set_log_mode()`. `VIDEOSDK_LOG_NORMAL` keeps the lifecycle, warning and error lines; `VIDEOSDK_LOG_DEBUG` adds the periodic heartbeats and diagnostics. Call it before [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init).

#### Updates

- Two new result codes: `DATA_CHANNEL_NOT_STARTED` (3025) means [`sendMessage()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#sendmessage) was called before the channel was opened, and `DATA_CHANNEL_QUEUE_FULL` (3026) means messages are being queued faster than they can be sent. See [Result Code](/iot/api/sdk-reference/result-code).
- [`sendMessage()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#sendmessage) now accepts up to `24000` bytes per message, down from `60000`.

#### Fixes

- Building a bundled example no longer shows the board and VideoSDK menus twice in `menuconfig`.

---

## v0.2.2

**Release Date** : 1st July 2026

#### Breaking Changes

- [`startSubscribeAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startsubscribeaudio) no longer takes arguments.
- `audio_codec_t` temporarily offers only `AUDIO_CODEC_PCMA`. PCMU and Opus return in v0.3.0.

#### Features

- **Video support.** Send camera frames to the room, and show remote video on boards with a display. Choose the format with the new `init_config_t.videoCodec` field, either `VIDEO_CODEC_NONE` or `VIDEO_CODEC_JPEG`. Receiving video needs a board with a display; see [Supported Microcontrollers](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/supported-browser-and-device-os). See also [Publish Video](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/handling-video/publish-video) and [Subscribe Video](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/handling-video/subscribe-video).
- [`setSpeakerVolume()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#setspeakervolume) changes playback volume while a call is running (on boards with a speaker; see [Supported Microcontrollers](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/supported-browser-and-device-os)).

#### Updates

- The component now pulls in everything the video path needs, so you do not have to add those dependencies yourself. The minimum ESP-IDF version is now **5.4**.

#### Fixes

- More reliable receive path, and fewer leaks over long sessions.

# Connection State - IoT SDK
A device may lose its Wi-Fi connection, move out of network range, or experience a network interruption long enough for the session to end. When this happens, the SDK notifies your application through a callback, allowing it to handle the disconnection gracefully instead of remaining in an unresponsive or partially connected state.

Two layers are involved, and they recover differently:

- **The network link.** Handled by whatever you use to bring up Wi-Fi, such as ESP-IDF's `example_connect()`. It reconnects on its own.
- **The VideoSDK session.** Reported by [`setConnectionStateHandler()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#setconnectionstatehandler). It does **not** come back on its own. Once the session drops, the device has to leave and join again.

- This callback is a **binary up/down signal for the signaling session**, nothing more. `connected == true` means the session joined or rejoined; `connected == false` means the signaling channel dropped and the session is dead.


### `setConnectionStateHandler()`

- The [`setConnectionStateHandler()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#setconnectionstatehandler) function registers a callback that fires whenever the signaling connection state changes. Register it after [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init). The current session state is replayed to your callback the moment you register, so a handler added late still learns whether the session is up or down, though registering before your `start*` calls guarantees you never miss a drop.
- Pass `NULL` as the callback to clear it.

This function takes two parameters:

- **cb**: a callback of the form `void cb(bool connected, void *user)`. A `connected == false` event means the session dropped.
- **user**: an opaque pointer handed back to the callback untouched. Use it to reach your own state, or pass `NULL`.

:::caution
The callback runs on an SDK task. Keep it short, and do not call [`leave()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#leave) from inside it, because `leave()` blocks until teardown finishes. Record the event and let your own task do the work.
:::

#### Example

```c
#include "videosdk.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
#include "freertos/FreeRTOS.h"
#include "freertos/task.h"

static volatile bool s_session_dropped = false;

static void on_connection_state(bool connected, void *user) {
  ESP_LOGI("IOT-SDK", "signaling connected = %d", connected);
  if (!connected) {
    //highlight-next-line
    s_session_dropped = true;   // flag it, handle it outside the callback
  }
}

// Register right after init(), before startPublishAudio() / startPublishVideo().
setConnectionStateHandler(on_connection_state, NULL);
```

## Rejoining after a drop

Once the flag is set, the recovery sequence is always the same: leave, then start a fresh session with [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init) and restart the streams you were running.

```c
static init_config_t s_init_cfg;   // keep the config you joined with

static bool rejoin_room(void) {
  result_t r = leave();
  if (r != RESULT_OK) {
    // STOP_PUBLISH_TASK_CREATE_FAILED / STOP_SUBSCRIBE_TASK_CREATE_FAILED:
    // teardown never started, the session is still up, so call leave() again.
    // LEAVE_FAILED: teardown is stuck. Do not rejoin on top of it.
    ESP_LOGE("IOT-SDK", "leave failed: %d", r);
    return false;
  }

  r = init(&s_init_cfg);
  if (r != RESULT_OK) {
    ESP_LOGE("IOT-SDK", "re-init failed: %d", r);
    return false;
  }

  setConnectionStateHandler(on_connection_state, NULL);
  startPublishAudio();
  // ...and any other direction this device was running.
  return true;
}

void app_task(void *arg) {
  int backoff_ms = 1000;
  while (1) {
    if (s_session_dropped) {
      s_session_dropped = false;
      if (rejoin_room()) {
        backoff_ms = 1000;                              // recovered
      } else {
        //highlight-next-line
        s_session_dropped = true;                       // try again later
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(backoff_ms));
        if (backoff_ms < 30000) backoff_ms *= 2;        // back off, do not hammer
      }
    }
    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(100));
  }
}
```

:::note
Back off between attempts. A device that retries in a tight loop while the network is still down burns power, floods your logs, and reconnects no faster.
:::

:::caution
If [`leave()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#leave) returns `LEAVE_FAILED`, teardown started but did not finish, so the session is not left cleanly. Do not immediately rejoin on top of it. Log it, and let the device restart with `esp_restart()` if it keeps happening. See [Result Code](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/result-code).
:::

## What to watch for

- The token is checked when the session is created. A token that expired while the device was running will make the rejoin fail rather than the original join, so long-lived devices need a way to obtain a fresh token. See [Authentication and Tokens](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/authentication-and-tokens).
- Turn on debug logs while you are testing recovery, so you can see the drop and the rejoin in the monitor. See [Logging and Debugging](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/logging-and-debugging).

- [leave](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#leave)

# Publish Audio - IoT SDK

The audio publishing feature lets an IoT device stream audio into a room for real-time, two-way communication with other participants.

### `startPublishAudio()`

- The [`startPublishAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startpublishaudio) function initiates publishing audio data from your IoT device into the active room session.
- This function takes no parameters. The participant identity comes from the `participantId` you set once in [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init).

:::note
- You must call the [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init) method before invoking `startPublishAudio()`. If not, the function will return an `INIT_NOT_CALLED` result code.

- Only one audio-publish stream can run at a time. If audio is already publishing, calling this function again returns a `TASK_ALREADY_STARTED` result code. (Video publishing is independent and can run at the same time.)

- To stop only this stream without leaving, call [`stopPublishAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#stoppublishaudio); [`startPublishAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startpublishaudio) resumes it. [`leave()`](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/leave-room) tears down all publishing and subscribing when you exit the room.
:::

:::caution
The `participantId` must be unique for each participant in the room. If you leave it as `NULL` or an empty string in [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init), the SDK generates a unique one for you.
:::

#### Example

``` c 
#include "videosdk.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
void app_main(){
  //highlight-next-line
  result_t publish_result = startPublishAudio();
  ESP_LOGI("IOT-SDK", "Publish Result: %d", publish_result);
}
```

### `stopPublishAudio()`

- The [`stopPublishAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#stoppublishaudio) function stops publishing audio without leaving the room. Call [`startPublishAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startpublishaudio) to resume. It is safe to call when audio is not being published.

#### Example

``` c
#include "videosdk.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
void app_main(){
  //highlight-next-line
  result_t stop_result = stopPublishAudio();
  ESP_LOGI("IOT-SDK", "Stop Publish Result: %d", stop_result);
}
```

- [startPublishAudio](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startpublishaudio)
- [stopPublishAudio](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#stoppublishaudio)

# Subscribe Audio - IoT SDK

The Audio subscribing feature allows IoT devices to receive and render audio streams from other participants in a room. This enables real-time playback of audio from remote peers in your VideoSDK-powered applications.


Playback needs a board with a speaker; without one, [`startSubscribeAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startsubscribeaudio) returns `DEVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED`. See [Supported Microcontrollers](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/supported-browser-and-device-os) for which boards support this.


### `startSubscribeAudio()`

- The [`startSubscribeAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startsubscribeaudio) function lets your device receive and play audio from the other participants in the room.

- This function takes no parameters. The participant identity comes from the `participantId` you set once in [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init).

:::note
- You must call the [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init) method before invoking `startSubscribeAudio()`. If not, the function will return an `INIT_NOT_CALLED` result code.

- To stop only this stream without leaving, call [`stopSubscribeAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#stopsubscribeaudio); [`startSubscribeAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startsubscribeaudio) resumes it. [`leave()`](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/leave-room) tears down all publishing and subscribing when you exit the room.
:::

:::caution
The `participantId` must be unique for each participant in the room. If you leave it as `NULL` or an empty string in [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init), the SDK generates a unique one for you.
:::

#### Example

``` c 
#include "videosdk.h"
#include "esp_log.h"

void app_main() {
  // Ensure init() is called before this
  //highlight-next-line
  result_t subscribe_result = startSubscribeAudio();
  ESP_LOGI("IOT-SDK", "Subscribe Result: %d", subscribe_result);
}
```

### `stopSubscribeAudio()`

- The [`stopSubscribeAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#stopsubscribeaudio) function stops playing remote audio without leaving the room. Call [`startSubscribeAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startsubscribeaudio) to resume. It is safe to call when audio is not being subscribed.

#### Example

``` c
#include "videosdk.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
void app_main(){
  //highlight-next-line
  result_t stop_result = stopSubscribeAudio();
  ESP_LOGI("IOT-SDK", "Stop Subscribe Result: %d", stop_result);
}
```

The API references for all the methods utilized in this guide are provided below.

- [startSubscribeAudio](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startsubscribeaudio)
- [stopSubscribeAudio](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#stopsubscribeaudio)

# Publish Video - IoT SDK

The Video publishing feature lets an IoT device capture frames from its on-board camera and stream them into a room, enabling real-time video alongside audio in your VideoSDK-powered applications.

### `startPublishVideo()`

- The [`startPublishVideo()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startpublishvideo) function initiates publishing video captured from your IoT device camera into the active room session.
- This function takes no parameters.

:::note
- You must call the [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init) method before invoking [`startPublishVideo()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startpublishvideo). If not, the function returns an `INIT_NOT_CALLED` result code.

- Set `.videoCodec = VIDEO_CODEC_JPEG` in [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init).

- Video can only be published once. Calling this function again while video is already publishing returns a `TASK_ALREADY_STARTED` result code.

- Both supported boards can send video. If the camera fails to initialize (ribbon unseated, or the wrong board selected in `menuconfig`), it returns `INIT_BOARD_FAILED`, not `DEVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED`. See [Supported Microcontrollers](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/supported-browser-and-device-os).

- To stop only this stream without leaving, call [`stopPublishVideo()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#stoppublishvideo); [`startPublishVideo()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startpublishvideo) resumes it. [`leave()`](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/leave-room) tears down all publishing and subscribing when you exit the room.
:::

#### Example

``` c
#include "videosdk.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
void app_main(){
  //highlight-next-line
  result_t publish_video_result = startPublishVideo();
  ESP_LOGI("IOT-SDK", "Publish Video Result: %d", publish_video_result);
}
```

### `stopPublishVideo()`

- The [`stopPublishVideo()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#stoppublishvideo) function stops publishing camera video without leaving the room. Call [`startPublishVideo()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startpublishvideo) to resume. It is safe to call when video is not being published.

#### Example

``` c
#include "videosdk.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
void app_main(){
  //highlight-next-line
  result_t stop_result = stopPublishVideo();
  ESP_LOGI("IOT-SDK", "Stop Publish Video Result: %d", stop_result);
}
```

# Initialise Room - IoT

To configure a VideoSDK room you require two things, first the `token` which will be used for **Authentication** purpose and a `roomId` which will be used to specify where a participant will join. Let's see each of the steps closely.

### Generating Token

You can generate a `token` in two ways:

1. **`Temporary Token`** : You can visit [Dashboard's API Key section](https://app.videosdk.live/api-keys) and generate the temporary token from there.

2. **`Server`** : You can setup **JWT** in backend and make an API call to get the token from your server.

To learn more about **Authentication** and token in detail you can follow [this guide](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/authentication-and-tokens).

import GenerateToken from "@site/src/theme/GenerateTokenContainer";

<GenerateToken />


### Generating Room Id

For generating the roomId you can use the function present in the IoT Sdk which is `create_room` which will return `create_room_result_t`. 

- `create_room_result_t` contains two fields: 
     1. Result Code
     2. room_id 

:::note  
If there is any error in the code, the function will stop performing its task and it will return the result code defined in [`result_t`](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/result-code) (please refer to this) in such cases, it will return `NULL` in `room_id`.  
:::

```c
char * token = "Generated token from Dashboard/API";
create_room_result_t result = create_room(token);
if (result.room_id) {
  ESP_LOGI("IOT-SDK", "Created room roomId = %s", result.room_id);
  free(result.room_id);
} else {
  ESP_LOGE("IOT-SDK", "Failed to create room");
}
```

### Initialization of Room
- This function initiates the VideoSDK IoT client with the configuration provided in an `init_config_t` structure.
- If the initialization succeeds it will return 0; otherwise it returns an error. 
:::note
- [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init) must be called **exactly once**, before starting publish or subscribe operations.

- Call the SDK from a **single task** (for example `app_main`). The API is not thread-safe, so do not call these methods concurrently from multiple tasks.
:::
```c
init_config_t init_cfg = {
      .roomId = "Your room id ",
      .token = "your authentication token",
      .displayName = "ESP32-Device",
      .participantId = "your participant id",   // "" or NULL => a random id is generated
      .audioCodec = AUDIO_CODEC_PCMA,           // PCMA, PCMU or OPUS
      .videoCodec = VIDEO_CODEC_JPEG,           // or VIDEO_CODEC_NONE for no video
      .signalingBaseUrl = NULL,                 // NULL => api.videosdk.live (default)
  };

init(&init_cfg);

```

:::tip
Register your callbacks right after [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init) and before the `start*` calls, so early events are delivered. Use [`setDataMessageHandler()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#setdatamessagehandler) for incoming messages and [`setConnectionStateHandler()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#setconnectionstatehandler) for signaling connection changes.
:::

- **`RoomId`** :

  - RoomId is unique identifiers that allow participants to join a specific room.
  - It will be in the format of `xxx-yyy-zzz` and will be generated using the [create_room method](#generating-room-id) or [VideoSDK's Room API](/api-reference/realtime-communication/create-room).

- **`token`** :
  -  A unique token allocated for each user by the videosdk.
  -  This token allows to authorize room participants.

- **`displayName`**:

  - This will represent the name of the participant in the room.
  - It accepts a `char*` value. If you pass `NULL` or an empty string, the SDK generates one for you.

- **`participantId`**:

  - The participant identity used for the whole session, shared by audio, video, subscribe and the message channel.
  - It accepts a `char*` value. If you pass `NULL` or an empty string, the SDK generates a random ID for you.
  - Each participant in a room must have a unique `participantId`.

- **`audioCodec`**:

  - An audio codec is a software component that encodes and decodes digital audio data.
  - This enum `audio_codec_t` defines the supported audio codecs, where PCMA and PCMU are standard telephony codecs, and OPUS is a modern codec optimized for real-time audio.

```c
typedef enum {
  AUDIO_CODEC_PCMA = 0,   // G.711 A-law, 8 kHz mono
  AUDIO_CODEC_PCMU,       // G.711 u-law, 8 kHz mono
  AUDIO_CODEC_OPUS,       // Opus
} audio_codec_t;
```
  :::tip
  The audio codec can be configured via `audio_codec_t`.
  Example: `.audioCodec = AUDIO_CODEC_PCMA`
:::

- **`videoCodec`**:

  - Declares the video format used when video is published. The `video_codec_t` enum defines the supported video codecs. Use **`VIDEO_CODEC_JPEG`** to enable video; `VIDEO_CODEC_NONE` (the default) is audio only.
  - See [Publish Video](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/handling-video/publish-video) to stream the device camera.

```c
typedef enum {
  VIDEO_CODEC_NONE = 0,   // audio only (default)
  VIDEO_CODEC_JPEG,       // hardware-JPEG camera frames
} video_codec_t;
```
  :::tip
  Set `.videoCodec = VIDEO_CODEC_JPEG` when you plan to publish or subscribe to video.
:::

- **`signalingBaseUrl`**:

  - Optional and advanced. Points the SDK at a different VideoSDK API host (host only, no port or path).
  - Leave it `NULL` (or omit it) to use the default host, `api.videosdk.live`.

### Example code 

```c

void app_main(void) {
  /*This function allow us to create a Room ID with the help of the token and
  on passing the wrong token it returns an error "Failed to created room"
  */
  char * token = "Generated token from Dashboard/API";
  //highlight-next-line
  create_room_result_t result = create_room(token);
  if (result.room_id) {
    ESP_LOGI("IOT-SDK", "Created room roomId = %s", result.room_id);
    free(result.room_id);
  } else {
    ESP_LOGE("IOT-SDK", "Failed to create room");
  }
/* this function allow us to create a room by authenticating
  the roomId, token, audioCodec and dislayName */
  //highlight-next-line
  init_config_t init_cfg = {
      .roomId = "your room id",
      .token = "your authentication token",
      .displayName = "ESP32-Device",
      .participantId = "your participant id",
      .audioCodec = AUDIO_CODEC_PCMA,
      .videoCodec = VIDEO_CODEC_JPEG,
      .signalingBaseUrl = NULL,   // NULL => api.videosdk.live (default)
  };

  //highlight-next-line
  init(&init_cfg);

  while (1) {
    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));
  }
}

```

- [init](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init)

# Logging and Debugging - IoT SDK

When a call does not work on a device, the serial monitor is all you have. The SDK ships two log levels, and getting the noisy one requires two separate things: the debug logs must be **compiled into the image**, and they must be **turned on**.

## Log levels

[`videosdk_set_log_mode()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#videosdk_set_log_mode) selects how much the SDK prints. Call it once, before [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init), so it covers the join.

```c
typedef enum {
  VIDEOSDK_LOG_NORMAL = 0,  // lifecycle, warnings and errors
  VIDEOSDK_LOG_DEBUG,       // adds periodic heartbeats and diagnostics
} videosdk_log_mode_t;
```

It only moves the SDK's own log tags. ESP-IDF and other components keep whatever level they were built with, which is `CONFIG_LOG_DEFAULT_LEVEL`.

Since v0.4.0, **Debug** mode also emits video-receive diagnostics, which help when remote video is not appearing.

## Turning debug logs on

Pick the level in `menuconfig` and read it back in code, so you can flip verbosity without editing source:

```
d. VideoSDK Logging
       |-> Log verbosity
             |-> Normal (default)
             |-> Debug
```

:::warning
Debug logs are only present in the image if the build allows that level. Keep this line in `sdkconfig.defaults`:

```bash
CONFIG_LOG_MAXIMUM_LEVEL_DEBUG=y
```

It costs a few KB of flash and turns nothing on by itself. Without it, selecting **Debug** prints nothing extra and it looks like the setting is broken.

Remember that `sdkconfig.defaults` is read only when no `sdkconfig` exists yet. If you add the line to a project you have already built, delete the generated `sdkconfig` and build again.
:::

## Reading the monitor

```bash
idf.py -p <PORT> monitor       # connect to the device's serial monitor
idf.py -p <PORT> flash monitor # flash the firmware and start the serial monitor
```

Exit the monitor with `Ctrl+]`. See [Quick Start](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/quickstart/quick-start) for how to find `<PORT>` on your machine.

A healthy audio join looks roughly like this, with `0` meaning `RESULT_OK`:

```
I (1180) IOT-SDK: [APP] Startup..
I (1190) IOT-SDK: [APP] IDF version: v5.4.2
I (4210) IOT-SDK: Device ID: esp32-a0b1c2d3e4f5
I (7480) IOT-SDK: init: 0
I (7910) IOT-SDK: startPublishAudio: 0
I (8020) IOT-SDK: startSubscribeAudio: 0
```

Any non-zero number is a [result code](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/result-code). Look it up there before guessing: several of them describe a configuration problem rather than a network one.

`startSubscribeAudio: 3004` or `startSubscribeVideo: 3004` on a send-only board is `DEVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED`, which is expected, not a failure. See [Supported Microcontrollers](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/supported-browser-and-device-os).

## Checking memory

Several result codes mean an allocation failed rather than a network problem: `MEMORY_ALLOC_FAILED` (3003), `PUBLISH_MEMORY_ALLOC_FAILED` (3012), `SUBSCRIBE_MEMORY_ALLOC_FAILED` (3016), and the mutex and task-creation failures. When you see one, print what is actually left:

```c
#include "esp_heap_caps.h"
#include "esp_system.h"

ESP_LOGI("IOT-SDK", "free heap: %u", (unsigned)esp_get_free_heap_size());
ESP_LOGI("IOT-SDK", "free internal: %u",
         (unsigned)heap_caps_get_free_size(MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL));
ESP_LOGI("IOT-SDK", "free PSRAM: %u",
         (unsigned)heap_caps_get_free_size(MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM));
```

If free PSRAM reads as `0`, PSRAM is not actually enabled and every media buffer is competing for internal RAM. Check that `CONFIG_SPIRAM`, `CONFIG_SPIRAM_MODE_OCT` and `CONFIG_SPIRAM_SPEED_80M` survived into your `sdkconfig`, and that the board really has octal PSRAM. See [Quick Start](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/quickstart/quick-start), Step 5.

## API Reference

- [Result Code](/iot/api/sdk-reference/result-code)

import ResultCodes from '../../../data/\_result-codes.mdx'

# Result Code - IoT SDK

Every SDK call returns a [`result_t`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/result-code). `RESULT_OK` (`0`) means the operation succeeded; anything else tells you what went wrong and, in most cases, what to do about it. On a device there is no exception to catch and no user watching, so check the return of every call and log it.

```c
result_t r = startPublishAudio();
if (r != RESULT_OK) {
  //highlight-next-line
  ESP_LOGE("IOT-SDK", "startPublishAudio failed: %d", r);
}
```

## How to read a failure

Codes fall into a few groups, and each group wants a different response.

- **Expected on this hardware.** `DEVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED` (3004) from a subscribe call means the board has no speaker or no display. Not a failure, and retrying will not change it. See [Supported Microcontrollers](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/supported-browser-and-device-os).
- **Wrong call order.** `INIT_NOT_CALLED` (3023), `DATA_CHANNEL_NOT_STARTED` (3025) and `TASK_ALREADY_STARTED` (3008) are programming errors. Fix the sequence rather than retrying.
- **Out of memory.** The allocation, mutex and task-creation codes mean the device ran short of RAM. Check what is actually free before you retry. See [Logging and Debugging](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/logging-and-debugging).
- **Network and transport.** `SSL_CONNECT_FAILED` (3001), `CANDIDATE_PAIR_FAILED` (3020) and `DTLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILED` (3021) mean the device could not reach or negotiate with the server. Retry with backoff, and suspect the network itself if they persist.
- **Session already gone.** If the session dropped mid-call, rejoin instead of retrying the call that failed. See [Connection State](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/connection-state).

:::caution
[`leave()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#leave) is the one call whose failures need opposite responses. `STOP_PUBLISH_TASK_CREATE_FAILED` (3018) and `STOP_SUBSCRIBE_TASK_CREATE_FAILED` (3019) mean teardown never started and the session is still up, so call `leave()` again. `LEAVE_FAILED` (3022) means teardown got stuck, so do not treat it as a clean exit.
:::

# Troubleshooting - IoT SDK

Start from what you can see: the compiler error, the boot log, or the number a call returned. Each entry says what causes it and where the full explanation lives.

:::tip
Turn on debug logs before chasing anything runtime related. `menuconfig` -> **VideoSDK Logging** -> **Debug**, and check `CONFIG_LOG_MAXIMUM_LEVEL_DEBUG=y` is in your build. See [Logging and Debugging](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/logging-and-debugging).
:::

## The build fails

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Incompatible pointer type errors coming from `srtp.c` | On Xtensa with ESP-IDF 5.4.2+, `uint32_t` is `long unsigned int` while libsrtp uses `unsigned int`. Same width, but the compiler rejects the pointers. | Add the `idf_component_get_property` / `target_compile_options` lines to `main/CMakeLists.txt`. Without them the project does not build. See [Quick Start](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/quickstart/quick-start), Step 3. |
| Build fails for a target other than ESP32-S3 | The SDK supports the ESP32-S3 only. | `idf.py set-target esp32s3`, then build again. |
| The app partition is too small for the binary | The default partition table does not fit the firmware. | Add `partitions.csv` and keep `CONFIG_PARTITION_TABLE_CUSTOM=y`. See [Quick Start](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/quickstart/quick-start), Step 4. |
| Undefined references when linking the component | An early SDK release did not declare its own runtime dependencies. | Move to the current release. See [Release Notes](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/release-notes). |


## Configuration does not take effect

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Values in `sdkconfig.defaults` are ignored | `sdkconfig.defaults` is read only on the first build, when no `sdkconfig` exists yet. | Delete the generated `sdkconfig` and build again. |
| **Debug** log verbosity is selected but nothing extra prints | The debug logs were never compiled into the image. | Keep `CONFIG_LOG_MAXIMUM_LEVEL_DEBUG=y` in `sdkconfig.defaults`, delete `sdkconfig`, rebuild. See [Logging and Debugging](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/logging-and-debugging). |
| Free PSRAM reads `0` at runtime | PSRAM is not actually enabled, so every media buffer competes for internal RAM. | Confirm `CONFIG_SPIRAM`, `CONFIG_SPIRAM_MODE_OCT` and `CONFIG_SPIRAM_SPEED_80M` survived into `sdkconfig`, and that the board really has octal PSRAM. See [Supported Microcontrollers](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/supported-browser-and-device-os). |

## Flashing and the serial monitor

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No such port, or you cannot tell which port is the board | The board enumerates differently per OS and per board. | List ports before and after plugging the board in. See [Quick Start](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/quickstart/quick-start), Step 8. |
| Permission denied opening the port on Linux | Your user is not in the `dialout` group. | `sudo usermod -a -G dialout $USER`, then log out and back in. |
| The port is busy | Another monitor or serial tool still holds it. | Close the other session. Exit a running monitor with `Ctrl+]`. |

## The device does not join

Check the number the call returned before guessing: it usually says which layer failed. Full table in [Result Code](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/result-code).

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The log says the token or room ID is not set, and the app returns early | `menuconfig` -> **VideoSDK Configuration** was never filled in. | Set the auth token and the room ID there. They live in `sdkconfig`, not in source. |
| `create_room()` or a `start*` call returns `3001` or `3002` | TLS or HTTP to the VideoSDK server failed. `init()` does no network I/O, so these surface when a room is created or the first `start*` opens signaling. | Confirm Wi-Fi is up and DNS resolves, and that the mbedTLS certificate bundle options are still set. Retry with a delay. |
| A `start*` call returns `3011` or `3015` | The peer connection never came up. | Verify the token is valid and unexpired, that the room ID exists, and that the network allows outbound UDP. |
| A join returns `3020` | ICE found no working network path, typically guest Wi-Fi or a captive portal blocking UDP. | Test on a phone hotspot to confirm, then fix the network. |
| A join returns `3021` | The DTLS handshake failed. | Retry. If it repeats, check free heap and that only one session is active on the device. |
| Any `*_MEMORY_ALLOC_FAILED`, `*_MUTEX_CREATE_FAILED` or `*_TASK_CREATE_FAILED` | The device ran short of RAM rather than hitting a network problem. | Print the free heap and confirm PSRAM is on. See [Logging and Debugging](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/logging-and-debugging). |
| A call returns `3023` | [`init()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#init) was not called first. | Call `init()` once, before any other SDK method. |

## Audio or video is missing

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `startSubscribeAudio()` or `startSubscribeVideo()` returns `3004` | The board has no speaker or no display. Expected, not a failure. | Use a board with that hardware, such as the ESP32-S3-Korvo-2. See [Supported Microcontrollers](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/supported-browser-and-device-os). |
| The device joins but other participants hear nothing | Publishing was never started, or it failed. | Check the return of [`startPublishAudio()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startpublishaudio) in the log. |
| Nothing plays through the speaker | Volume is at zero, or the wrong board is selected. | Set the speaker volume in `menuconfig` -> **SET Microcontroller**, or call [`setSpeakerVolume()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#setspeakervolume) at runtime. |
| `startPublishAudio()` or `startSubscribeAudio()` returns `3010` | The board's I2S/codec (mic or speaker) driver did not come up. | Confirm the board under `menuconfig` -> **SET Microcontroller** matches your hardware, check the mic or speaker is wired and responding, and check free internal RAM. |
| `init()` (audio codec, Korvo-2) or a video `start*` call (camera/display) returns `3006` | Board hardware that should be present failed to start. | Confirm the board selected under `menuconfig` -> **SET Microcontroller** matches the hardware you are flashing, and that the camera ribbon is seated. |
| Video never appears | The device is audio-only, or the camera was not detected. | Set `init_config_t.videoCodec` to `VIDEO_CODEC_JPEG` and check the camera sensor options in `sdkconfig.defaults`. See [Publish Video](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/handling-video/publish-video). |

## It works, then stops

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The call goes quiet after a while and never recovers | The signaling session dropped. Wi-Fi reconnects on its own, the session does not. | Register [`setConnectionStateHandler()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#setconnectionstatehandler) and rejoin. See [Connection State](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/setup-call/connection-state). |
| A device that ran for hours fails to rejoin | The token expired while the device was up. | Give long-lived devices a way to fetch a fresh token. See [Authentication and Tokens](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/authentication-and-tokens). |
| `sendMessage()` returns `3026` | The send queue is momentarily full. | Slow down, and retry shortly. See [Send Message](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/data-channel/send-message). |
| `sendMessage()` returns `3025` | The channel was never opened. | Call [`startMessageChannel()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#startmessagechannel) once after `init()`. |
| [`leave()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#leave) returns `3018` or `3019` | Teardown never started, so the session is still active. | Free some memory and call `leave()` again. |
| [`leave()`](/iot/api/sdk-reference/Methods#leave) returns `3022` | Teardown started but did not finish in 6 seconds. | Do not treat it as a clean exit and do not rejoin on top of it. Restart the device if it repeats. |

## Still stuck

Collect the serial log with debug verbosity on, note the SDK version from your `main/idf_component.yml` and the ESP-IDF version printed at boot, then reach out:

- [Discord](https://discord.gg/f2WsNDN9S5)
- [GitHub](https://github.com/videosdk-live)
- [Talk to an expert](https://www.videosdk.live/contact)

# Supported Microcontrollers 


Media support depends on the board's hardware. The **[ESP32-S3-Korvo-2](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-adf/en/latest/design-guide/dev-boards/user-guide-esp32-s3-korvo-2.html)** has a microphone, speaker, camera, and display. The **[Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/xiao_esp32s3_getting_started/)** is a send-only board with no speaker or display, so its subscribe calls return `DEVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED`.

Both boards can send and receive [Data Channel](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/data-channel/send-message) messages.

| Board | Send audio | Receive audio | Send video | Receive video | Send and receive messages |
| --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| [XIAO ESP32-S3 (Sense)](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/xiao_esp32s3_getting_started/) | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| [ESP32-S3-Korvo-2 v3.1](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-adf/en/latest/design-guide/dev-boards/user-guide-esp32-s3-korvo-2.html) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

# IoT SDK

The IoT SDK brings VideoSDK's real-time audio, video, and messaging to embedded devices. It is written natively in C and runs on ESP32-S3 microcontrollers, so your hardware can join a room and interact with other participants just like any other VideoSDK client.

## The Architecture

A device running the IoT SDK joins a VideoSDK room as a participant. Once it is in the room, everything the platform already does for browser and mobile clients applies to the device too, and every other VideoSDK client can see and talk to it.

![IoT SDK Architecture](https://strapi.videosdk.live/uploads/iot_usecase_architecture_8a5777d06f.jpeg)

- **Your device** runs the IoT SDK on an ESP32-S3 board. It publishes audio and video, subscribes to other participants, and exchanges messages over the data channel.
- **VideoSDK infrastructure** hosts the room the device joins. Because the device is a normal participant, platform capabilities such as live streaming, recording, and session analytics operate on that room. These run on the platform, not on the microcontroller.
- **Control platforms** are your web, mobile, and desktop apps built with any other VideoSDK client SDK. They join the same room to view the device's streams and send it commands.

What the IoT SDK itself implements on the device:

- **Media**: publish and subscribe to audio and video, subject to what the board's hardware supports.
- **Data channel**: send and receive messages alongside media, which is how control commands, sensor readings, and status updates travel in both directions.

## Supported Boards

The **[ESP32-S3-Korvo-2](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-adf/en/latest/design-guide/dev-boards/user-guide-esp32-s3-korvo-2.html)** has a microphone, speaker, camera, and display. The **[Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/xiao_esp32s3_getting_started/)** is a send-only board with no speaker or display, so its subscribe calls return `DEVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED`.

| Board | Send audio | Receive audio | Send video | Receive video | Send and receive messages |
| --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| [XIAO ESP32-S3 (Sense)](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/xiao_esp32s3_getting_started/) | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| [ESP32-S3-Korvo-2 v3.1](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-adf/en/latest/design-guide/dev-boards/user-guide-esp32-s3-korvo-2.html) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

Both boards can send and receive [Data Channel](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/data-channel/send-message) messages. Both need **8 MB flash** and **octal PSRAM**.

See [Supported Microcontrollers](/iot/guide/video-and-audio-calling-api-sdk/supported-browser-and-device-os) for the full detail.
